notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0162.stoa047a.opp-l: ab2 'De brevi Proverbio edito' is obscure as a heading; translated literally. Prologue: 'flamma' (from water) is taken as a corruption of 'phlegma', phlegm, as the humour scheme requires. The four 'stars' are the Greek words for north (arktos), west (dysis), east (anatole) and south (mesembria), whose initials spell ADAM; the scanned forms are corrupt. 'ponant' is read as 'portant', carry. 'domun excelsum' is read as 'donum excelsum'. 'quatuor evangelistae Mat.' breaks off; the text is evidently incomplete. Jacob's third supplanting repeats 'per benedictionem', apparently an error in the text. 'qui at -, antra patrem habemus Deum' is garbled; it is read as 'quia et nos patrem habemus Deum'. In 1.3, 'per Christi gen.' is abbreviated in the edition and taken as 'generationem'. In 1.4, 'factus ex Spiritu Spiritus' looks corrupt; the reading is uncertain. In 1.5, the edition conjectures 'coitionem' (intercourse) for 'creationem' and 'ininterpretatum' (left uninterpreted) for 'interpretatum'; the first conjecture is followed, and the second is left as printed. 'excelsum dicitur nobiscum Deus' is unclear. In 1.6, 'Juda est respice Bethlehem gentium' is obscure and possibly corrupt; translated literally.

Text heavily corrupted by scanning throughout. Line 7: 'confessionum' reflects the etymology of Judah as 'confession'. Line 8: 'clam loca'i' read as 'clam vocatis'; the clause on Herod 'thinking a son was born from him' is obscure. Line 9: the sentence on the Saviour led on high (the temptation) is elliptical and its subjects uncertain. Line 10: the gospel's 'sixtieth' fruit appears here as 'quadragesimus' (fortieth); translated as given. Line 12: 'Noctem hic ostendit, quod secessit litterae tenebrae' is garbled; 'et non pervenit usque ad mortem' is obscure. Line 13: 'oMit' read as 'ovis' (sheep). Line 14: 'weci' read as 'caeci' (blind). Line 15: 'ad regem Archelaum' obscure; perhaps 'not to be reckoned from King Archelaus'. Line 16: the threefold crying passage and the clause on the belt ('pia ibi cit') are corrupt; locusts called 'birds' as in the text.

The text is badly scanned throughout; evident readings have been translated. Line 18: 'Sarabatae' is taken as Sarabaites. Line 19: 'patricidas et matricidas viperas ... simulam' is taken as 'simulant', with 'occulerunt' as 'occiderunt'. Line 20: 'radices fiii, arborum, perantum' is read as 'filii ... parentum'. Line 23: 'Sinc modo' is read as 'Sine modo'. 'ab undis Christus, vel martyrio, ad te pervenit' is obscure. 'ita baptismus mari' is unclear; it may be 'Christi'. 'hic It.. nitas' is read as 'Trinitas', and 'Mam' as 'Adam'. Line 26: 'non est, ut a capite...' is obscure; my rendering is conjectural. 'pel membrum a Pilato' is read as 'per membrum'. Line 29: the sentence about Deuteronomy and David is garbled. Line 30: 'in tia' is read as 'in via'. 'pinguedo sanguine caret' is uncertain.

31: 'in V cLeri' read as 'in Vetere'; 'offeret' has no object, '[himself]' supplied. 33: the last sentence ('nam his duobus : aliis fuit non sua') is elliptical; the sense given is conjectural. 34: 'bis quatuor' and the 'quadriga' image are obscure. 38: 'in altitudinem mandatorum descendere in deserto' seems to have lost a verb such as 'ascendere'; 'incarnationem' is odd here, perhaps for 'divinitatem'. 39: 'credo videret' is probably a garbled 'Credo videre bona Domini in terra viventium' (Ps 26:13); 'amara, pro peccato non flere' appears corrupt ('non' likely an error); 'a jacent a caelo' read as 'cadentes/venientes a caelo', uncertain. 41: only three pairings are listed for 'four parts'. 42: 'septem mulieres unum virum' alludes to Isaiah 4:1. 45: 'Moyses et Levi tres gladios' is unclear (cf. Exodus 32); 'vetas' read as 'vetus'. 46: the passage on iota and 'deca' is confused in the text: iota is the Greek numeral ten; translated as it stands.

The text is heavily corrupted by scanning; evident readings adopted throughout (e.g. 'Iladium' read as gladium, 'rade' as vade, 'tote' as sole, 'fetam vkam' as praesentem vitam, 'mille repet' as ille regnet, 'picem' as panem). In 51 the two kinds of desire are obscurely worded; the sense 'inclination follows but deed does not' may be intended. In 53 'alter est, est' presumably stands for 'sit sermo vester est, est'. In 64 'in terra, id est, in caelo' is elliptical, and the allegorical list (gold, the senses; the world, clothing) is uncertain in its pairing. In 66 'reparationem divinitatis' and 'Idem per charitatem' are unclear and possibly corrupt.

67: 'figs, that is, a spouse' (conjugem) is odd but translated as printed. 68: 'OMntes' read as 'orantes' (praying). 69: the lemma ('everyone who hears my words and will not do them') does not fit the following comment on the leper's cleansing (Matt. 8:1–4; Lev. 14); the text seems to have lost the lemma here. 'nam ascendat' read as 'ut ascendat'. 70: 'natus esset a lepra' read as 'sanatus' (healed); 'sub lectum' read as 'sub tectum' (roof); 'comersi' read as 'conversi'; 'Why with three only' refers presumably to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. 71: 'Ades' read as 'fides'. 73: 'MiMis pannis' read as 'veteribus pannis' (old cloths). 74: 'Cautarimus... ei non saltasti tibias' is garbled; read as 'we piped/sang to you and you did not dance'. Four kinds of praise and four kinds of calling are announced, but the first praise is unlabelled and only three callings are given.

77: 'a quarta pars' read as 'a quarta parte'. 78: 'secutae ostendit pedestres' is elliptical (Matt. 14:13, the crowds following on foot). 81: 'divisi', 'justificati' are etymologies of the sect names. 84: 'a cornemium' is a scanning error, read as 'Cornelium' (Cornelius); 'in alium' perhaps for 'in altum'; 'Nec contemnatis unum etc fris' read as 'unum ex his'. 85: 'Non imago' perhaps for 'Non homo' or similar; sense uncertain.

87: 'Quatuor animae pereunt' explains only two persons; presumably the two women are understood. 89: 'vitae filia Sion' read as '[dicite] filiae Sion'; 'roUra' read as 'folia' (leaves); 'substitutionem' may be a corruption of 'superstitionem' (superstition); 'Mens' read as 'Mons'. 'Mons Oliveti, id est, nomen trium luminum' is obscure. 90: 'templum martyrium' is unclear, possibly 'templum, martyrium' or a corruption. 93: 'in spiris pinnis' read as 'expansis pinnis'.

94: 'in opere justitiis' (the one left) is odd and may be corrupt; translated as 'in works of justice'. 97: the text appears to have lost something before 'immunditiam purgaret'; marked [...]. The sentence about Adam and the Jews stretching out hands is repeated in the edition with 'in lignum vitae' and 'in ligno crucis', apparently garbled; translated as printed. 98: 'Hyrus b Pompeius est' is evidently corrupt; rendered conjecturally as 'hircus emissarius' (scapegoat), which fits Barabbas led into the desert. 'Gazophylacia' taken as gazophylacium (treasury). 105: the printed text repeats 'per diem vero prosperitatem, sive ignorantiam ostendit' before the correct 'sive scientiam'; this dittography is omitted. 'Lucerna sub mudiot' read as 'sub modio'.

106: 'auctus mittebat' read as 'fluctus mittebat'. 107: the edition repeats 'propter serpentes, id est, pro cupiditate mentis aut infidelitate', evidently by dittography; translated once. 'ad t'OSt' read as 'ad vos'; 'inter iidem' as 'inter fidem'. 109: 'in pristino a corporis sui' seems to have lost a word (perhaps 'statu'). 'sine prius saturare' read as 'sine'. 112: after 'per stridorem dentium' the explanation is missing in the text; marked [...]. 'pater infanti' read as 'pater infantis'. The quotation is Ps 48:8 (Vulgate). 113: 'quam et alii a regno Dei disturbent' is grammatically awkward; rendered by sense. 116: 'b ras' read as 'vas'; 'aui' as 'ad'. 'Venit ad synagogam, synagoga sepe custodia angelorum' seems garbled; 'sepe' is taken as 'sepes' (hedge, Mark 12:1), but the reading is uncertain.

117: 'Terrae motus ... audiendi verbum Dei' is elliptical and may be corrupt; rendered as best the sense allows. 119: 'per genitorem' read as 'per janitorem' (doorkeeper, cf. Mark 13:34). 121: 'uana' read as 'nunc', 'vinuli' as 'vini', 'Pro quid' as 'per quod'; 'ostendit se cum discipulis ad Judaeos' is obscure. 122: 'circumdato Christi Ecclesia' is garbled; rendered loosely as 'Christ encompassed by the Church'. 124: 'vitem' read as 'vitam'. 126: 'ipse consurgens' is odd and possibly corrupt. 127: 'de vice Abia, id est, in diebus Domini' is obscure. 128: 'idem primum rugat' read as 'id est, primum rogat'; 'testimonium majus fuisset virtus' taken as 'so that the miracle would be a greater testimony'. 129: 'v millia saeculi' taken as five thousand years of the world.

Many scanning errors silently corrected (e.g. Cbristus, iaberna, nou, tegulas). Line 131: the material on Augustus, Tiberius, the bronze circle and the spring of oil is legendary and in places garbled; 'adsuerunt agnum mundi' is unclear and rendered with [...]; 'pater unitatem filii sui voluntatem' is ungrammatical and translated tentatively. 'taberna meritoria' (a Roman hostel for veteran soldiers, traditionally in Trastevere) is left untranslated. 'In tempore... completur baptismum suum' is confused. Line 130: 'sive L Maria benedicta, id est, a carne Christi' is obscure. Line 132: 'quod non reddendum' in 134 ('stetit') is uncertain. Line 134: 'lutum fabricando' presumably alludes to brick-making in Egypt. Line 135: 'tilia' read as 'filia' (the widow's daughter? probably the widow of Zarephath); the identification of Gehazi with the Church is as the text gives it. 'Per tres Leges' (133) is unexplained in the text.

137: 'a caudes ... cordis' and 'istae quatuor lenes' are corrupt; rendered as an etymology of 'cardinal' from cor, and the obscure word left as [...]. 'pdiebanL' read as odiebant. 138: 'naii suut' (angels) is corrupt and left as [...]; 'fiaxe' (sickness under air) unclear, left as [...]; 'Ire' read as Tres; 'Qui traHor' read as Qui minor. 140: the sentence 'navigantes ex polilia periculo navigii...' is corrupt; translated tentatively. 141: 'utram linguam' read as unam linguam. 144: 'interne habitat, vineam extet yiinat' is garbled; read as 'dwells within and destroys the vineyard'.

145: 'in carmen' read as 'in carnem' (in the flesh). 'Mulier quaedam, id est, divitias' (riches) may be a corruption of 'divinitas' (the Godhead). 'Quis rex, id est, apostolos' is odd and may be corrupt. 147: 'Si lapis moralia, id est, si gentiles a ut equus' is garbled; read 'lapis molaris' (millstone), and the clause after 'gentiles' seems lost. 148: 'judex et vidua de semiplenis' is obscure; 'et perierunt' (they perished) may be corrupt; 'in ipso corruit' is unclear. 150: 'filius, id est, virtutes: quod faciebat in die, in nocte ruebat' and 'novem servos, qui non negati sunt' are obscure and probably corrupt.

153: 'Leviathan A densi seduna' is corrupt and could not be construed; left as [...]. 160: 'cum a,.bore' read as 'cum arbore' (with the tree), sense uncertain; 'serpentis terei' read as 'aenei' (bronze); 'Mas' unidentified. 161: 'etaM lerventes' read as 'erant ferventes'; 'Mon eat tuus' as 'non est tuus'. 158: 'tertia lex' (third law) as printed; possibly a corruption.

166: 'me quod non fuit, nec habere' is corrupt; rendered as if a verb such as 'negavit' (denied) had dropped out. 167 'Manu dicitur apud Hebraeos' is obscure as transmitted. 168: 'a scripturae scriptura divina' is corrupt; probably originally glossed the door (ostium/janua) as divine scripture, and rendered so. 'qui fit utraque unum' read as 'qui fecit utraque unum' (who made both one).

169: 'Princeps' presumably refers to Caiaphas as high priest; 'causas dixit' is odd and may be corrupt. 170: 'tres secundum adventum' makes little sense ('the three'); perhaps a corruption (e.g. of 'justi', the righteous). The opening sentence about Mary's ointment ('ita et totus mundus quod intelligitur') appears garbled, perhaps anticipating the later 'totus mundus' clause. The edition marks a lacuna after 'Christus'. 171: the passage from 'ex Judaeis revelatum ex gentibus' onward appears to run Isaiah 53:1 into John 12:44 without a transition; it is translated as it stands. 173: '(Incipit capitulatio.)' and 176: '(Explicit Passio.' are rubrics from the edition or manuscript; the bracket opened in 173 is not closed in this stretch. 177: 'per bis spiritum acceptum' is read as 'the Spirit received twice'; the text may be corrupt. Scanning errors silently corrected throughout.

181: 'notum feci omnibis apud te' is garbled; translated literally. 'sed illa visa est Ostiaria' is unclear; rendered as referring to the doorkeeper. 186: 'diligebat mundum' is read as 'Dominum' (the Lord); the printed text says 'the world'. 'tibi non ascendi' is taken as 'nondum ascendi' ('I have not yet ascended'). 'per tres' is unexplained in the text. 187: 'ja- ollis' is read as 'januis' (doors). 'sine mem' is truncated and the sense 'without hindrance' is a guess. The clause about being 'whole and incorrupt in marriage' is obscure and seems to refer to John. 188: badly corrupted. 'opusparatum' is read as 'opus paratum' ('the work prepared'). This reflects the tradition that John was the bridegroom at Cana. The sentence on the order of the canon is grammatically incomplete. Throughout, many scanning errors have been silently corrected.

nodes.text: THE APPENDIX TO THE WORKS OF ST EUSEBIUS JEROME OF STRIDON, PRIEST, CONTAINING SPURIOUS WRITINGS.
PART THREE: COMMENTARIES ON THE NEW TESTAMENT.
EXPOSITION OF THE FOUR GOSPELS
On a short published proverb.
PROLOGUE.
First, for all books, one must ask about the time, the place and the person; and why, out of twelve

Gospels, only four are received: because the whole world consists of four elements, that is, heaven, earth, fire and water. By heaven John is shown: because as heaven surpasses all things, so too does John, who said: In the beginning was the Word. By earth, Matthew, who said: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ. By fire, Luke, who said: Was not our heart already burning within us? By water, Mark, who said: The voice of one crying in the desert. That is, the four rivers from one spring signify the four evangelists; [the spring] is Christ. Pishon, 'insufflation', signifies John; Gihon, 'swiftness', signifies Matthew; Tigris, 'happiness', signifies Mark; Euphrates, 'fruitfulness', signifies Luke. They water the world, that is, the Church, and they signify the four virtues, that is, prudence, temperance, fortitude and justice: and as four rivers water paradise, so these four virtues [water] our heart. And man consists of four elements: of air, fire, water and earth. From air, breath; from fire, blood; from water, phlegm; from earth, the body. By the head, heaven, where there are two lights; by the chest, air; by the belly, water; by the feet, earth. Likewise Adam took his name from four stars, that is, arctos, dysis, anatole and mesembria; or they signify the four evangelists. And as every man is born from Adam, so through the four evangelists all come to faith. Likewise Noah's ark is read to have been square, made of timbers, its length three hundred cubits, its width fifty, its height thirty, and finished in one cubit: it signifies the Church. Through the four evangelists the length is hope of eternal life, the width charity, the height faith in the Trinity, and the one cubit is to worship one Lord. The pitch inside and outside signifies love of God and of neighbour. Likewise the ark of the covenant, in which were the two tablets and the rod of Aaron, was carried by four golden rings; and the poles covered with gold signify the four evangelists: the ark is the Church, the poles the teachers. As those were enclosed by the rings, so [are] the priests taught in the Old and New Testament. The four evangelists carry the Church, defending it from heresy. By the rod the cross is shown: and as a squared timber stands firm whichever side it is turned on, so a man taught by the four evangelists becomes firm against heresy and tribulation. Likewise Matthew [means] 'given'; Mark 'lofty gift'; Luke 'rising up'; John 'grace of the Lord'. Likewise the wheel within a wheel and the spirit in the wheel: [the wheel is] the preaching of the Gospel turning in the world; the Spirit in the wheel is the Holy Spirit in the Gospel. Likewise the linen vessel and the four lines on it signify the four evangelists: these are the clean and the unclean, Jews and Gentiles. Likewise the four living creatures have eyes before and behind, crying 'Holy': the four evangelists, Matthew [...]. Likewise Jacob supplanted his brother three times: first through the blessing, second through the lentils, third through the blessing. Esau signifies the devil, Jacob Christ, who conquered and supplanted him three times: so we too ought to supplant our brother the devil three times, in thought, in word and in deed. He is our brother for this reason, that God created him, [and] we too have God as father: and He created him good, but by his own fault, through pride, he deprived himself. The four evangelists signify: Matthew the face of a man, Luke of a calf, Mark of a lion, John of an eagle. The Lord Jesus Christ fulfilled the whole: a man by being born, a calf by being sacrificed, a lion by rising, an eagle by ascending. Wheel within wheel: law within law, the old within the new. Why are the four Gospels written not by four apostles but by two disciples and two apostles? Because the sons of Jacob were born of two free women and two maidservants. Matthew is honey, Mark milk, Luke oil, John wine.
ON THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MATTHEW.

The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham. He names two fathers because of David it is said: Of the fruit of your womb I will set upon your throne; of Abraham it is said: In your seed all nations shall be blessed. David is written before Abraham because he is nearer to Christ, Christ being born of that stock. Jacob begot Joseph: he spoke according to [natural] begetting; Luke spoke according to the law, so that he would be the son of Heli. Women are in the genealogy of Christ because they come to eternal life as men do; and sinners are named in the genealogy of Christ because he himself said: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners. Luke, speaking of Christ back to Adam, shows that through the generation of Christ Adam is loosed from sin, or that those who go out from Christ are those who return to the Father. The figure of forty-two [generations] in the genealogy of Christ is the forty-two stations of the sons of Israel from Egypt to the land of promise, that is, from the world to heaven: which signifies coming to Christ by three kinds, through faith, hope and charity. What [is meant] by fourteen, if not the ten words of the Law and the four virtues? The first, prudence: to serve God, not idols; the second, temperance: not to covet; the third, justice: not to commit adultery; the fourth, fortitude: to forgive, not to kill. Through four came the ruin of the world: through a man, through a woman, through a tree, through a serpent; and through four it is restored: through Christ, through Mary, through the cross, through the man Joseph. The serpent that was in Israel signified Christ: it was made of bronze with four round wheels, and those who looked on it were healed. And he raised it up on the top of a pole, so that all might see it, and the beasts of the desert fled for fear of the wheels; and so each one is healed if he looks at Christ on the top of the pole, that is, on the cross. The four wheels signify the four evangelists: so the devil flees the Gospel when it sounds out to heaven.

Now the generation of Christ was thus. That is, according to the flesh, they said. It says 'of Christ' so that from that derived word they may be called Christians; again, by etymology, 'Christ' means 'anointed', because through it, after the washing, we have received the anointing of chrism. 'Was thus' through eternity. 'Mary' means 'star of the sea': because a star is sweet, the sea bitter; so Mary was in the sea of the world among sinners like a star of the sea: because, as is the custom, a star leads men to harbour if they follow it; so [was] Mary in the world, where Christ was born, who leads all to life if they follow him. His mother was betrothed: that is, for four reasons: so that she would not be stoned as an adulteress, and so that she would have comfort in the flight, and [so that] the genealogy of Christ [would run] through Joseph, and so that the birth would be hidden from the devil. Before they came together: that is, before they were in one dwelling. She was found by Joseph [with child] in the womb: not in the vulva, as a woman, but as a virgin, having of the Holy Spirit: that is, made from the Spirit, [by] the Spirit, just as he makes fruit on the tree, and [made] Eve from the bone of Adam.

Now Joseph her husband: he is called her husband, and called just, so that others would not suspect a human union. He was unwilling to expose her: that is, in court, lest he transgress the law: because he knew [her to be] a virgin; so that her childbearing might be hidden from the devil. But while he thought on these things: that is, he was considering whether to dismiss or to keep [her]. Here the prophecy is fulfilled: A helper in times of need, in tribulation. An angel of the Lord said in dreams. Not 'in a dream', because the angel came to him quite often in dreams; not once, because the mystery of God cannot be known at once. Joseph, son of David: that is, the prophecy through David fulfilled in Joseph, Of the fruit of your womb, and the rest. Do not fear: that is, love and rejoice in [her as] a wife, not a bride for wedlock; not intercourse, but living together. He said 'your', so that he would believe [the child] was conceived not by another but of the Holy Spirit. She will bear a son: that is, so that he would have greater joy over a son, as is the custom among men. And you shall call his name: again, so that it might be for his gladness. Jesus: as if he had said 'Saviour'. He will save his people: he did not say all, but those who believe in him. From their sins: that is, what no other physician could do. Now all this was done: that is, what the angel said: so that what was said by the Lord might be fulfilled: that is, through the prophet Isaiah about Christ; here [it is] only according to the letter. Behold, a virgin shall have in the womb, and shall call his name Emmanuel: this name has been interpreted, because in both languages it is loftily called 'God with us', that is, God and man, that it may be in one faith. He did as the angel commanded him: it shows that he who did as he commanded him deserved to see the vision of the Lord.

And he did not know her until she bore her son. 'Until' is said for 'never'. In the law, 'firstborn' is said of him who first opened the womb: not one whom [other] sons follow, but who is born first. Christ is called firstborn for three [reasons]: in the resurrection from the dead, and from Mary, and from [among] the creatures. So when Jesus was born: he confirms three things, place, time, person. In Bethlehem: it was fitting, because it is interpreted 'house of bread', so that the living heavenly bread might be born there. Judah is 'look upon the Bethlehem of the Gentiles'. In the days of Herod the king: that is, he refers to the kings and leaders of Judea, as was said: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it was promised; he will be the expectation of the nations. He named Herod king against the Jews because they said at the cross: We have no king but Caesar. Behold, magi come from the East: since it is the East who is sought, he is therefore made known from the East; he leads us to himself. They came to Jerusalem: because out of Sion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Saying, where is he who has been born king of the Jews? That is, king of confessions. They add the reason for those asking, 'Who told you?': for we have seen his star in the East: a mute star, but bright; the light leads to the Word. Again, 'his star', and not [the star] of heaven and earth, nor was it theirs, but the Son of God's. Neither afterwards nor before was there [one] like Christ in the flesh; therefore a star [led] them, so that a heavenly [thing] might lead heavenly [men] to the heavenly one: and therefore no other creature but a mute one, so that a mute [thing] might lead mute [men] to the mute one. They bring gifts, who used to worship idols. King Herod was troubled: that is, through envy, lest he should surpass him and his sons: or else all feared lest it should not go well for them. When a just king is with an unjust king, the companions of a king are not so dear with another king: or they were troubled for this reason, so as to please the king. Again, according to the letter, a good showing becomes a disturbance to the wicked, and an evil eye is troubled by the rising of the sun.

And gathering all the chief priests and scribes of the people: that is, hoping, when they had come, that he might receive counsel, as God [says]: Ask your father, and he will declare to you, your elders, and they will tell you; the fathers [are] the chiefs of the elders and the scribes. Where Christ would be born. He did not say 'where was he born, where is he?' But they said, in Bethlehem of Judea: in words they say what they deny in deeds; the blind feel about, as Isaac [felt] Jacob, while they neglect to go [to him] whom they point out to be worshipped. The three magi, [like] the three sons of Noah, with three gifts, signify the worship of the Trinity. Then Herod, secretly [calling them]: here the narrative falls short, since it indicates the time of the star in secret; on account of this opinions differ as to when the magi came. For some say [it was] after one or two years: [and that] they found him not in Bethlehem but in Egypt; and if in twelve days, how could they have come from a distant land, Persia or Havilah, Arabia or Kedar, in twelve days? But God can do this, at whose word rocks fly and mountains will move, whose nature it is that what he commands comes to be. He learned diligently from them the time of the star: that is, so that he might know at what time: perhaps he thought that a son had been born from him, or from his own line.

When they had heard the king, they went away. When he sends [them] to seek Christ, he is to be listened to: and when he orders [them] to return to him, he is to be disregarded. For when he led the Saviour up on high, he refused [it], he did not refuse [to go]: but when he sends him down and orders him to worship him, he refused according to the law: You shall worship the Lord your God, and the rest. So they, going out, know how to go out, [but] do not know how to return. And behold, the star which they had seen, and the rest. It is uncertain where it hid itself when they went away. [There is] something of human counsel: because the Lord hides from our hearts, so that it may also be sought out. The star: faith, or the law? The compunction which leads us to Christ went before them; when they came to Christ, the star led them through: for the star did not lead them to Herod. Herod signified the devil, because whoever goes out from the devil's suggestion goes to Christ with the star of faith. Seeing the star they rejoiced, and the rest: because it is the custom of all to rejoice when what was lost is found. Therefore he shows also the child [as] more exalted than his mother.

And entering the house, and the rest: [was it] a house or an inn? And falling down they worshipped him: before, they used to worship a star: the creature ceased while the creator is worshipped. And opening their treasures, and the rest: gold for a king, frankincense for God, myrrh for the tomb. Whether one offered gold, another frankincense, the third myrrh, is not known: or whether each offered three gifts, is not said openly, but both [are meant] figuratively. They do not disagree, because three faithful are one, and in one there would be three fruits, the thirtieth, the fortieth, the hundredth: the thirtieth in the faith of the Trinity, the fortieth in the perfection of the active life, the hundredth in the contemplation of eternal life. Each offered three [things]: through gold a pure conscience, through frankincense right prayer, through myrrh the mortification of the will. Again, the three gifts [are] holy thought, good word, and perfect deed. The star thus appeared only at his birth, as the dove at the baptism. For the star, when it went before them, [was] not far from the earth.

And having received an answer in sleep, and the rest. [It was] in sleep, with the eye closed, so that they might worship the invisible and incomprehensible God, and so that [their] waking eyes might be opened not to creatures but to the creator. That they should not return to Herod: that is, after penance, to the devil. They returned by another way to their own country. The country is paradise. He goes back by another way who amends his whole life and comes from depravity to holiness.

When they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord, and the rest. Gabriel is called 'strength of God'. It was fitting that the strength of God should strengthen the weakness of humanity. And otherwise: because the angel draws near to us when we have withdrawn from Herod, the devil. He fled into Egypt: the flight shows victory, as with Joshua son of Nun when he said: Divide yourselves, and take to flight until the citizens come out of doors; afterwards turn back, and you will conquer them. Christ first flees, until afterwards he conquers the devil. So Joseph in Egypt fled from his illustrious mistress, and afterwards he himself ruled over Egypt. And [be there] until I tell you: here he shows that the devil is not always to be fled, as the apostle Paul says: Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Here he shows night, because the darkness of the letter of the Law has settled among the Jews after Christ up to today. And until the death of Herod: he waits, that is, three years: it signifies that the Gentiles would believe in the Trinity. And it does not reach to the death. Herod indicates the Jews, who come to Christ after the death of the letter of the Law. Out of Egypt I have called my son: first Moses and Aaron call forth Christ.

Then Herod, seeing that he had been mocked by the magi. Here the prophecy is fulfilled: this dragon which you formed to mock him. And he sends and kills all the boys, so as to find the newborn king: here he is mocked the more: those whom he thought destroyed, he sent alive into paradise. From two years old and under: that is, from the past and the following year, because 'infancy' is the name for two years. A voice in Ramah, and the rest. Rachel is interpreted 'sheep' or 'seeing God'; Ramah, 'lofty'. Rachel [is] the Church, which weeps in the valley of tears for those it lost, who sinned before, for whom it will not be consoled, because they are not Christians. Rachel was the mother of Benjamin; or else because she died and was buried there, where the little ones were killed. For they are dead, and the rest. Therefore [it is] synecdoche, the part for the whole.

He came to the city of Nazareth: that is, 'flower of cleanness'; it was fitting for him to live there who said: I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys. Archelaus, 'lion searching'; Nazarene, 'holy'. Arise, take the child and his mother. First, arise from the earth, you who leave earthly things. And he orders [him] to take the child first, afterwards the mother: rather, to love God first, afterwards the neighbour. Archelaus [is] heresy: those who think themselves to be what they are not, and are blind.

In those days. It is not to be said [as] to King Archelaus, but from the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar; because in that very year the word of the Lord came upon John, before Christ: the voice before the Word, the lamp before the sun, the flower before the fruit. Do penance, and not 'work', because works are said [to concern] bodies outwardly; 'do' [it] in the inner man: let it be done from the heart. True penance is to weep for what has been lost, and not to commit what must be repented of.

For the kingdom of heaven has drawn near: that is, baptism, or the Gospel of Christ, martyrdom, or the Church. The voice of one crying in the desert: John's crying for Christ happens in a threefold manner: if [the hearer] is far off: Salvation is far from sinners; second, to the deaf: Like the deaf asp, and the rest; third, it is indignant: that is, your fury has been indignant. In the desert: that is, without law, without king, without priest or prophecy were the Jews. As those who love [their] friend join a bride to [him as] spouse, so John joined the Church to Christ. Therefore he is called the friend of the bridegroom. John had a garment of camels' hair: he was born in fasting, and had the clothing and food of fasting; it was fitting, since he taught penance, that he should first fulfil it in himself, so that everyone who preaches the word should confirm it by example. John's clothing from camels signifies the Church of the Gentiles, or their riches, which Christ gathered, and it becomes the Church. The belt, that is, the mortification of vices: about the loins, that is, because there is the fornication of man, and of women in the navel. His food locusts: they are most wretched birds; they show the Jews, who use the letter of the law like locusts; wild honey signifies the sweet words of God, or the Jews who received the sweet preaching and came to Christ.

Then they went out to him Jerusalem, and the rest. That is, the land of Judaea: it is said for its inhabitants. Jerusalem, 'vision of peace', indicates the peaceable, who come to Christ through confession. Jordan, that is, 'descent', signifies those descending in humility to Christ.

And they were baptized in the Jordan: it shows that the humble came to baptism through descent. Confessing their sins: it shows that one must confess sins before one comes to communion. Pharisees, that is, 'divided', or they are called Sarabaites; Sadducees, 'justified in their own eyes'.

And he said to them: Brood of vipers. The same poison is only in the tongue; for the Pharisees and Sadducees imitate vipers, killers of father and mother, who killed their mother the synagogue, and [their] fathers and the prophets. Who showed you, and the rest: that is, 'who' is said not of possibility but of difficulty; bear good fruits, that is, lay aside every vice; or bear fruit worthy of penance, that is, let him who has two tunics give to him who has none; let those who do unlawful things abstain from unlawful things.

God is able from these stones, and the rest. They were stones, because they worshipped stones, but many from there came to faith in Christ. That is, they resemble stones, because they are heavy and hard and cold in faith. The axe is laid, that is, the Gospel; to the root of the trees, that is, to the Jews. An axe consists of iron and wood: so Christ of divinity and humanity; roots, thoughts; of trees, of sinners; or roots, sons; of trees, of parents.

Every tree which does not bear good fruit will be cut down: that is, it will be divided from the Church. It will be thrown into the fire, that is, on the day of judgement. He is stronger than I: that is, Christ is stronger not only than John but than all; stronger for this reason, because he baptizes in the Holy Spirit and in fire. To carry [his] sandals: therefore I cannot recount his incarnation more fully.

He will baptize you with fire: that is, in the judgement, or in the Holy Spirit and fire. Whose winnowing-fan, and the rest: that is, just judgement; in his hand, that is, in his power; the threshing-floor, that is, the world or the Church; the wheat, that is, the holy; into the barn, into the kingdom of heaven; the chaff, sinners, because chaff is light and is carried by the wind, and fire burns it: so sinners themselves keep the fire [going], because the fire does not fail, since the wood does not fail.

Then Jesus came to Galilee to be baptized, and the rest. Christ came to John: that is, the bride kisses the bridegroom, because through John the bridegroom belongs to the Church. Here it says: Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth. Or Christ is baptized by John for this reason, that a servant should not excuse himself from being baptized by his Lord, nor the Lord disdain to be baptized by his servant. I ought to be baptized by you. For this reason John recognised Christ among many, when the Jordan fled from him and the mountains leapt: because the creature recognised the Creator; and therefore he came to John, to cleanse the waters and to be shown forth by the Holy Spirit. Four reasons. Allow it now, that is, until both were baptized: that is, Christ by the waves, or [baptism] by martyrdom comes to you. All righteousness, and the rest: that is, the law of nature, or the law of the letter, because it was their custom to honour elders. The baptism of Christ: so that they should not distinguish the baptism of John from the baptism of Christ. Because water washes and quenches, therefore baptism was through waters: so John washes and quenches sin, gives life and satisfies: so too baptism [does]. And because they are baptized with two substances, that is, water and the priest's voice, visible and invisible, body and soul. He went up from the water: it signifies afterwards ascending by good works, and descending by the step of humility, because Jordan is called 'descent'. Behold, the heavens were opened, that is, it shows baptism: heaven is opened to each one after the fault of Adam. And he saw the Spirit descending like a dove: it shows that [it was] in the form of a dove only, because the Spirit received a body from it: the likeness of a dove was made for this, for before it did not exist. The Spirit came upon Christ in a dove for this reason, because it is a gentle bird: so Christ is gentle, without stain. For otherwise, the dove has seven figures: the sevenfold Spirit is signified; and therefore the Spirit came upon Christ through a dove, like the star, which neither existed before nor afterwards. Or for this reason, because the Son [was] in a body: because just as men could not have borne the presence of the Son of God without a body, so neither would they have borne the Spirit without the appearance of a dove. Why upon the apostles in fire, and upon Christ in a dove, they show must be explained according to the letter. And a voice from heaven: here the Trinity is compared: the voice of the Father, the Son, the Spirit through the dove. This is my Son, and the rest: because earlier the son Adam displeased, but in Christ he was well pleased.

Then Jesus was led, and so on: that is, led by the Holy Spirit into the desert after baptism: they show that the devil is conquered through fasting and prayer. We too ought to be led into the desert away from vices, so that we may conquer them. To be tempted by the devil, that is, that he might conquer the devil. Forty days and forty nights, so that heretics should not say that he ate at night. Forty [is] a sign, because Moses fasted forty [days] on the mountain, and Elijah forty; and he was with his disciples forty days after the resurrection; and the flood [was] of forty days, because by these he had to wipe away the sin of Adam. Afterwards he was hungry: it shows a true man, so that the devil might be deceived about his birth.

The tempter approaching: that is, like a fish he tests the hook, and is conquered: so that he who conquered the first man through gluttony might be conquered by the second through abstinence. If you are the Son of God, tell [these] stones, and the rest: by etymology, bread (panis) is from feeding (pascendo); [he wanted] to see whether he could do this from rock; or because, mystically, the devil's food [is] men who are stony and hard in sin; but he who produced wine from water and water from rock could have done this if he had wished.

Man does not live by bread alone, and the rest: that is, man would not have lived if God had not willed, even if he had eaten bread; and if he had not eaten bread, he would have lived if [God] had willed, like Moses and Elijah for forty days. The word of God [is life] for the soul, that is, eternal life. In the holy city, that is, Jerusalem; upon the pinnacle of the temple, that is, upon the wall of the enclosure of the court; they signify pride. It is no [wonder] that he let himself be tempted by the head who allowed himself to be crucified by Pilate, a member. These three temptations the devil first demanded of Adam: through gluttony he said, Taste; through vainglory, You will be like gods; through avarice, knowing good and evil. And through these three he again tempted Christ: by gluttony, to make bread from rock; by vainglory, Throw yourself down; by avarice, All this I will give you, and the rest. But he who leads him into the abyss by the word of preaching shows [how] to conquer the devil through these three. Here he shows true God and true man: the man whom the devil tempts is God, whom the angels served. Forty days are a tithe of the year, so that, just as we ought to give tithes of all things, so we should also strive to give God a tithe of the days of our life.

For [he has given] his angels [charge], and the rest: so that he might conquer Christ by an example, just as Christ conquered him by his own example through Scripture. But the devil does not understand that psalm rightly concerning Christ. Jesus said to him: You shall not tempt the Lord your God. Here he says: since I am the Lord your God, why do you tempt me?

And he showed him all the kingdoms of the world: that is, gold, silver. All these I will give you, and the rest. He truly falls who worships the devil; whatever monk serves a prince for reward makes himself the devil's slave. Go behind, that is, [into] your kingdom now, or at the judgement into hell.

You shall worship your Lord, and the rest: through three examples from Deuteronomy, by which the Gospel is signified, that is, the repetition of the law, the Lord conquered the devil. Likewise it signifies, that is, the temptation in David and Goliath: five stones, the five books of Moses; who killed the devil with one, that is, one book as a stone. Through three temptations, that is, suggestion, delight, consent; but he tempted Christ by suggestion alone, because suggestion comes from the devil.

Now when Jesus had heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee: that is, he went away from the Jews to the Gentiles; or, having left the synagogue with its Law, he established the Church and the Gospel. Galilee is called 'rolling': he came to those who come from bad to good; and because he came for the healing of the girl, and healed the woman on the way, it signifies the synagogue and the Church. Leaving the city of Galilee, he came into Capernaum: a most beautiful village, it figures the Church. Nazareth is called 'flower', because fruit comes from the flower; Capernaum, 'village of richness': light illuminates, and richness lacks blood. It shows that Christ passed from the flower of the letter of the law to the fruit of the richness of the Gospel places, that is, of knowledge. In the territories of Zebulun and Naphtali: Zebulun is called 'dwelling of beauty'; Naphtali is called 'forgetfulness'. Here it shows that he who forgets his sins dwells in beauty. Beyond the Jordan, and the rest: because out of fear of the Gentile peoples he stayed at night in the field. It saw a great light, as it says: Light has risen for those who sat in darkness, that is, of the ignorance of sins; light has risen for them, that is, Christ.

Do penance, that is, put wine on the wound; for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near, that is, oil on the wound: it gives consolation, because in the Old [Testament] they sacrificed livestock, in the New each one will offer [himself] to the Lord. He was walking: he shows us that we are in the present world by passing through, not by loving [it]. Beside the sea: in worldly flesh. The sea of Galilee is the same as the lake of Gennesaret, the lake of the salt-pans, and the sea of Tiberias, and the lake of Chinnereth.

Come after me, and the rest: that is, to draw souls from the open sea of sin to the shore of eternal rest; for it is the custom of fishermen to have a boat and a net on the sea: so the apostles [have] the Church [as the boat], the Gospels [as the net], and the world [as the sea], and men [as] the fish; casting nets into the sea [is] preaching into the world.

They, leaving their nets and their father, followed him. Likewise, [leaving] the father, the devil; the nets of their dwelling, and the business of the world. Peter and Andrew cast their nets into the sea: they show that the Lord chose some who were desirous, clinging to the things of the world. James and John were mending their nets so that they might cast them into the sea, that is, that he chose others desiring to cling to the things of the world. Which of these four left more? Peter and Andrew left more, because [the nets] were their own, for [they belonged] to these two; for the others, they were not their own.

I will make you, and the rest. He changed their disposition, not their occupation; but twice four: this is the first four-horse team. Now they are sent two by two into the Church, as into Noah's ark. The animals two by two signify the four virtues: justice, prudence, fortitude, temperance. The peoples were called through three callings: the first through John, to friendship: Behold the Lamb of God; the second, to belief, as John says: This first sign Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, so that his disciples might believe in him; the third calling, to apostleship: Come after me, and the rest.

Jesus went around all Galilee, and the rest. As Gideon conquered the Philistines, so Christ [conquered] the demons. Teaching, that is, the things that belonged to the law; preaching, that is, the Gospel. Every sickness, that is, he was the physician of the people, that is, of Israel: sickness of the body, infirmity of the soul.

And his fame went out into all Syria: that is, into all nations. All who were ill, that is, they were insane with many sins, or with bad faith. And because they had demons: that is, in the soul idols are believed in. Lunatics, that is, the lunatics thought their infirmities came from the rising of the moon.

They brought him paralytics: that is, those sluggish in doing good. And great crowds followed him, that is: first the disciples, for faith; second the sick, for healing; third those learned in the law, to find fault; fourth the poor, for alms; fifth the women, so that they should not despair; sixth [the crowd] of little children, as he said: Let the little children come. Decapolis: that is, those who keep the words of the Law; and from Jerusalem, that is, that seeing peace they followed Christ; and from Judaea, that is, those who followed Christ through confession.

Jesus, seeing the crowds. Likewise four crowds followed Christ, and the same four follow the Church: the first, [who came] to Christ through fear and love, likewise come to the Church; the second, those [who come] out of desire for food or drink; the third, out of envy, to have something to accuse; the fourth, the teachers. Christ had three refuges to flee the crowds: on the mountain, in the desert, in the boat on the sea. These three he leaves to us: [to ascend] to the height of the commandments; to go down into the desert, to forsake vices; and to enter into the unity of the Church. The boat signifies the Church: as it has a helmsman and sailors, and those who throw out the water from the boat, so [the Church has] bishops, and workers, and those who perform the ministries within. And boats encounter three [dangers]: danger in the waves, in the wind, on the rock; so the danger to the Church is in the waves, of the devil's temptation; in the wind, of sins; on the rock, from false brethren. When he went up the mountain, he signified the theoretical, that is, the contemplative; when he came down, he teaches the practical, that is, the active. And when he had sat down: it shows that his incarnation [i.e. divinity] did not appear, because he who sits covers his body with his garment.

His disciples came to him: that is, body and soul. And opening his mouth, that is, he who opened the mouths of the prophets. Blessed are the poor in spirit, that is, those who are poor for the sake of the Holy Spirit, though they could be rich. Blessed are the meek, that is, he who returns evil for evil to no one; for they shall possess the land, of which it is said: I believe [I shall] see, and the rest. Blessed are those who mourn now: he does not say this of every weeping, but of three, which [those in] the world ought to have: first, weeping for one's own sin; second, for a neighbour's sin; third, for heavenly love. Tears have three natures: bitter, [for the one who weeps] for sin; warm, to weep for a neighbour's offences through the warmth of charity; [the third,] coming from heaven, to weep for love of it. Tears are shed for three causes: for remembrance, for fear of the future, for exile.

Blessed are those who hunger, and the rest: that is, he for whom whatever good he does is not enough, but he wants to do more. They shall be filled, that is, in the kingdom of God. Blessed are the merciful: that is, those who show mercy are freed from misery, and will go to heaven with their gift. Blessed are the clean of heart, that is, those [who are] of pure heart; [such a one] is not touched by any consciousness of sin, because the clean God looks upon the clean of heart.
Blessed are the peacemakers: that is, in four directions: between God and man, and neighbour; between a man and his friend. One must hate the vice and love the man.

Blessed are those who suffer persecution for justice's sake, that is, in Christ. These eight beatitudes pertain to the eight persons who were in the ark, and ought to be now, because seven women had one man, Christ: that is, in the resurrection. These eight beatitudes are fulfilled in Christ. Blessed are the poor in spirit: The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. Blessed are the meek: Learn from me, for I am meek. Blessed are those who mourn: Seeing the city, he wept over it. Blessed are those who hunger: My food is to do the will of my Father. Blessed are the merciful, that is: I desire mercy, and not sacrifice. Blessed are the clean of heart, that is: Be holy, for I am holy. Blessed are the peacemakers: My peace I give you, and the rest. Blessed are those who suffer persecution, that is: If they have persecuted me, they will persecute you too.

You are the salt of the earth: that is, the apostles and teachers are so called; 'of the earth' means of this world. But if the salt has lost its savour, and the rest. If the teacher goes astray, by whom is he corrected? Salt gives flavour [and] kills worms. Let it be thrown out and trodden down by men, that is, let them go outside the Church and be reckoned among the Gentiles. You are the light of the world: that is, as light reveals what is hidden and illuminates darkness, so you too illuminate the darkness of sins. In another sense, as the sun always remains in the sky, so you too remain there.

A city cannot be hidden: that is, the Church, on a mountain, that is, on Christ. Nor do they light a lamp, that is, the apostles and teachers. They do not put [it] under a bushel, that is, under fear, or love. The apostles have four likenesses: salt, sun, lamp, city. On a lampstand, that is, the Church. So that they may give light to all who are in the house: that is, in the Church, or in the world. So let your light shine, that is, teaching, or good works. And may they glorify your Father, that is, in your good deeds.

Do not think that I have come to abolish the law: that is, whatever work was done, he himself fulfilled. When the children of Israel sinned, Moses and Levi took up three swords for vengeance upon them, which Christ did when he said: I have not come to send peace, but a sword. And to fulfil, that is, what was lacking; because the old Law ordered that anyone who committed adultery be punished, but now it is not abolished but fulfilled when it is said: Whoever looks at a woman to desire her, and the rest; and again: For every idle word [men will] render account on the day of judgement. See, I have not come to abolish the law, but to add what the old [law] did not say.

Amen I say to you. Amen, that is, truly, or faithfully. One iota, the name of a letter made with a single stroke: it becomes the letter 'deca', that is, the ten words of the Law; among the Greeks [it is] a letter which we have called 'one'. One tittle, one point, according to the letter; but according to the sense, the least commandments of the Law. Until all things are done: because the things that were least in the law are full of mysteries; the iota is the old Law, the tittle the New.

For whoever abolishes one of these least commandments: that is, he who teaches much and fulfils very little. The Pharisees strain out a gnat and swallow a camel: that is, he who preaches the least things to others and commits greater ones himself. He shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven, that is, in the Church. Unless your justice abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees: because they taught great things and did little, or because they rejected other commandments of the law: what they did not love they did not speak of, and what they loved they spoke of.

You have heard that it was said to the ancients, You shall not kill; that is, not to abolish the law. Whoever is angry with his brother: that is, anger in the heart without voice, shall be liable to judgement, that is, on the day of judgement. Raca, that is, empty or vain. Fool, that is, without brains: shall be liable to the fire of Gehenna, that is, Gehenna is a double punishment, because it punishes soul and body.

If you offer your gift at the altar, and the rest: go to be reconciled to your brother: that is, the gift, [whether] prayer, offering, or you offer yourself for communion: one must never come to the Church until you are reconciled to your brother. Leave your gift there: how will this be fulfilled? He rebukes both alike; if [the brother] is near, well, and if far away, one must nevertheless be reconciled in mind, and [do] what has already been said, to have peace with all men.

Agree with your adversary, that is, the Gospel: while you are on the way with him, that is, in this life; or with your adversary the devil, that you do not do what he suggests to you, lest punishment be increased for you for your sin. If an infant asks for a sword, do not hand him [something] with which he may stab himself: and thus you agree with him. Lest perhaps the adversary hand you over to the judge, that is, lest the law of the Gospel hand you over to Christ the judge, because you did not agree with the Gospel; to the officer, that is, the angel who sends souls into punishment; into prison, that is, into hell.

You will not come out from there, that is, because no one comes out of hell, until he pays the last farthing: 'until' is taken for 'always'. The quadrans is the fourth part of a coin, which is given as payment for bathing, or it is said for the smallest sin: to pay the farthing [is] to be sent into hell; or because man is made of four elements. You have heard that it was said to the ancients, You shall not commit adultery, that is, you shall not be an adulterer. Whoever looks at a woman to desire her. There are two desires: the first, which, if the opportunity follows, the inclination to the deed does not follow; the second, which is consummated if opportunity is at hand: [then] one has committed adultery in body, and it is done in the heart.

If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it from you. That is, your prince or teacher; pluck out, that is, separate him from you, if he has prohibited you from the service of God; one of your members, that is, it is better for you that the prince perish than that you go with him into hell. The eye, that is, your desire, because the body is sent into Gehenna through it. The right hand, that is, a servant, or your anger: causes you to stumble, that is, send it away from you: the hand, that is, an evil work: cut off.

Not to swear: that is, not to swear falsely; not to swear at all: that is, never to swear; neither by heaven, because it is the seat of God: let [your speech] be yes, yes; no, no, that is, a word is to be spoken in the mouth and in the heart: whatever is more than this is from evil, that is, from the unworthiness of the one who is not believed.

An eye for an eye, that is, not to return evil for evil. If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, that is, if a heretic strikes you in a doctrine of evil scripture, offer him another doctrine of divine Scripture, for living. Whoever wishes to take away your tunic, that is, to strip you of the charge that men sharpen against you: let go your cloak too, that is, of the crime of which you alone are aware, give him confession. And if anyone compels you [to go] a thousand paces, go with him another thousand, that is, if you have gone forth in body, go also in mind. Whoever asks of you, give to him, that is, whoever questions [you], tell him; or, give alms to the poor man.

It was said to the ancients, You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy. Just as he said, not to abolish the law, he rightly fulfils [it], because in the old [law] he says, concerning the devil, to hate the enemy; but here [he speaks] of both. In three ways we love enemies: with the heart, [him] who hates us in the heart; in deed, by doing good to him who persecutes us in deed; to pray, in word, [for those] who accuse us in word. Those who slander you, that is, false accusation. That you may be sons of your Father, and the rest: that is, as if someone had brought gold [and] silver to us, and if he had cursed us and struck us, we would love him; and when those things had failed, we too would have failed; therefore life that does not fail is promised. Who [makes] his sun, and the rest: and rains upon the just, because in both the whole world is contained: in the sun, the dry and the hot; in the rain, the moist and the cold: of these four the world is made. So we ought to give our enemies food and drink, clothing, and a word of love.

For if you love those, and the rest. A publican is so called because he sins publicly, or because he manages public affairs; heathens, gentiles. Be perfect, that is, so that you fulfil these things perfectly, in almsgiving, in fasting, in prayers: lest you be seen before men, that is, that good works not be done for human praise.

When therefore you give alms, that is, give to the priest, and to the poor man, and to the enemy. A hypocrite is called a pretender. They have received their reward, not God's. Let your left hand not know, that is, vainglory; the right: do all things for God's sake. Enter into your chamber, that is, into the secret places of the heart: having shut the door, that is, against vainglory.

Do not speak much, that is, not to make many petitions or say many words, or to ask God with loudness of voice. For the Father knows what you need. Pray then like this: Our Father, that is, let us so live on earth that we may have a father in heaven; we show charity and brotherhood when we say 'our'. The emperor says this, and the beggar; the lord says it and the slave; together they say: Our Father. Therefore those who have one father are brothers: so let the lord not disdain to have his slave as a brother, whom the Lord Christ willed to be a brother. And let us so act that we may be heirs of the Father; for human law too makes sons inherit.

Hallowed be your name: here we ask that it be hallowed in us, that is, in our works; for his name is always holy. Your kingdom come, that is, just as sons wish the kingdom for their father, so we also pray that he may reign in us, and not the devil: he, and not sin; or the Church, or the Gospel.

Your will be done, and the rest. Just as the angels in heaven serve without fault, so also we; or as in souls, so also in the body; or as [in] Christians, so [in] heretics; as [in] the Church, so [in] the Synagogue; as justice, so sin. Let them be converted, so that your will may be done in them.

Our daily bread: that is, every day until the end of the year; today, that is, always; bread, that is, Christ. We ought so to act that we may receive him daily as a remedy. And forgive us, and the rest: here we make a pledge with God: if you forgive, it will be forgiven you.
And lead us not into temptation. As you led astray men in the flood, or those in Sodom, or Pharaoh into the sea; or into the temptation of the devil, or the snares of men.

But deliver us from evil. That is, from the devil, from sin, from an evil man. These seven prayers [are] like the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: four are common to all; three petitions pertain to heavenly things, that is, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done; four to this present life.

When moreover they fast, and the rest: they disfigure their faces. That is, they transform themselves, that is, so that they may be seen by men, because they are fasting. Anoint your head and wash your face, that is, what you wish to give the Lord, who is your head, give to your neighbour. Do not store up treasure on earth, that is, [store it] in heaven: where rust, that is, vainglory, or anger; moth, envy or pride; thieves, demons; gold, the senses; the world, clothing; for food [is] divine preaching.

The lamp of your body: that is, your teacher or prince; of the body, that is, of the inner man; if it is single, [i.e.] of one thing. No one can serve two masters; where your treasure is, and the rest: either he will hate the one, that is, who is not good even to himself; he will love the other, who is good to himself: that is, to despise the devil, to love God. Whoever serves riches serves the devil. Riches are called mammon, or [it is] a name of the devil.

Is not the soul more than food? That is, [against] him who gives lesser things to God and greater to the devil. Look at the birds of the sky, and the rest. Because it is the custom of birds to fly on high and to sing a song, and whatever they want for themselves on earth they receive from the Lord: so men too ought to think on heavenly things and praise God; and when they need food, they receive on earth from the Lord the restoration of the divinity. How much more will your Father, who is good by nature, give good things to those who ask him, that is, the same through charity. Enter through the narrow gate, where sinners will not fit unless they lay down the burdens they carry. Two, that is, love of God and of neighbour; two lights, the upper the Gospel, the lower the old Law; where one offends, he does not enter. How wide the gate, and the rest: that is, those who serve riches and their own will.

Take heed for yourselves, that is, beware of false teachers: in sheep's clothing, that is, [the clothing] of a good teacher, ravening wolves, that is, they snatch souls into perdition. By their fruits, that is, from their works, you will know them, that is, do they gather from thorns, that is, from heretics, grapes, that is, virginity; from thistles figs, that is, a spouse from heretics? A good tree, a good man; a bad tree, a bad man, who does bad works.

Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, and the rest. He speaks of those who love to stand praying at the corners. But he who does the will of my Father, that is, who keeps the commandments. Many say to me, Lord, that is, many there are who enter by it: For I never knew you, that is, [as] good, or [they are] heretics. Depart from me, that is, those who hope that there is no forgiveness of sins. Everyone who hears my words, and the rest; who does not act against the preaching, will be likened to a wise man who built his house upon rock, that is, upon good work, so that the rain should not enter it, that is, the teaching of heretics; the floods, the persecutions of heretics; the winds, demons. The clouds take rain from the sea, heretics [take] teaching from the world. And the house did not fall, that is, he does not fall who stands upon faith in Christ.

And everyone who hears my words and will not do them. That is, it was the custom in the Law that one who was not clean should not be among the people, and if he had received health, he was to show himself to the priest; and a gift was offered for him: two turtle-doves or two young pigeons. And there was with them, beside this work, hyssop wood, and scarlet around the top of that wood, and the blood of one bird was sprinkled upon that wood [and] upon the other bird, and that [bird] was released into the air. The wood is the cross of Christ; the scarlet, his passion. And one must go to martyrdom through the passion of Christ, and our blood must be sprinkled upon his cross, so that it may ascend to the Church after the passion of our body in martyrdom.

As a testimony to them. That is, that he had not broken the law, or that they had seen that he had been healed of leprosy. The centurion figures teachers; the servant, paralysed and crippled, signifies the human race, shut up in sins. Jesus found three mysteries in the centurion: first humility, where he says, Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof; second faith, where he says, only say the word and he will be healed; third, that is, prudence, where he said, a man under authority. Jesus marvels at the centurion, that is, he found in him wisdom, in which he had been taught through divine preaching. Turned from the east, that is, from infancy; from the west, that is, from old age; from the south, from youth; from the north, that is, from the power of the devil, they come to faith; they will recline, that is, they dwell. Why with three only? That is, because of forgiveness. Those who covet will weep there: theirs is the gnashing of teeth, whose God is the belly. Peter's mother-in-law in a fever: that is, the doubt of the synagogue.

He touched the hand. He gave help, the fever having left, that is, unbelief ceases. She served him, that is, she blessed him; by the evening he showed her the end of the world. Demons, that is, sins; by the foxes, that is, unbelieving men; by the birds, rich men. He does not lay his head, where there is no faith. The dead burying the dead, that is, the body the soul; otherwise, if a sinner praises a sinner.

The ship, that is, of the Church; the motion and the waves, that is, temptation; sleeping, that is, incarnate, or crucified; the wind, that is, sudden temptation. The demoniac, the gentile, the nation with its faithlessness. Among the tombs, these are bodies; [no one] passes along the way, that is, through gentile ways to the kingdom. The herd of pigs shows men before conversion; plunged into the sea, that is, into the deep. By the herdsman he shows the philosophers.

He rose: that is, he was healed; returned to his house, that is, to the first creation. The bridegroom is Christ; the bride, the Church; the sons of the bridegroom are the Apostles. The raw cloth, the teaching of the Gospel; the old cloths, these are old men. New wine and old wineskins, new preaching to old men. The ruler holds the figure of the prophets, or of the patriarchs. This girl is the synagogue. Jesus held the hand of the same girl, that is, he gave her help. The harvest is great, that is, hearts are prepared; the reapers, teachers. Not two tunics, that is, not a double mind nor a double trust, in the New or in the Old Testament. No shoes, that is, not the testimony of evil men; nor a staff, that is, not by force, but through patience. Peace returned, that is, reward received; by the dust, defilement. These are so because dust hinders in three ways: it binds the steps, darkens the eyes, soils the clothes. A serpent when tormented hides its head, that is, the apostles when tormented, not denying Christ. Persecutions, these are heresies. From one city into another, that is, through the individual questions of the books.

Nothing is covered that will not be revealed: that is, the passion of Christ and of all teachers. What I say in darkness, that is, to the Jews, speak in the light, that is, in the Church. Two sparrows, that is, body and soul, or Christ and Barabbas. The penny, that is, faith; by the sword, this is the word of preaching. Otherwise, two sparrows, that is, the two Testaments. The penny, this is Christ. To separate father from son, this is the faithful from the unfaithful. Takes up the cross, that is, torment yourself. To be scandalised in Christ, that is, to deny Christ. A reed shaken by the wind, these are flattering men: empty, without fruit. The kingdom of heaven suffers violence, this is, because through torments of the flesh and of penance one comes to the kingdom of God. He is Elijah, who is John, because the same spirit was in Elijah at the second coming that was in John at the first coming. Children sitting in the market-place, these are the prophets. We sang to you with pipes and you did not dance, that is, we announced the coming to you, and you did not believe. We lamented and you did not mourn: we announced penance to you, you dreaded confession. Praises are in four ways: I will confess to you, Lord, Father of heaven; of faith: I believe in God the Father; of martyrs: Whoever confesses me before men; of sinners: Confess to the Lord, for he is good. You have hidden from the wise, that is, those who use the wisdom of this world; you have revealed to little ones, that is, to the disciples. The calling has been made in four ways: in the new: Come to me, all you who labour. In the old: Come, sons, hear me; in the future: Come, you blessed.

The yoke, that is, the teaching, is light to those who are willing, heavy to those unwilling [to bear] it. Perfection is understood in three ways, that is, of disciples, through baptism; of sinners, through forgiveness; of Jews, through the renewal of the New Testament. Through the sown fields, that is, the harvest, which signifies the old Law. The sabbath, the rest of the New Testament; the disciples plucking ears, that is, drawing testimonies from the Old to confirm the New; rubbing [them] in their hands, that is, pressing [them] out into the spiritual sense. The man with a withered hand shows avarice, one who is greedy in taking, miserly in giving. Let him who used to steal learn to give. He stretched out his hand, that is, with the heart purged it was restored; it signifies conversion to faith. The smoking wood, that is, the hearts of the gentiles prepared for faith. A man possessed by a demon, mute and blind, signifies the human race. In the house he bound the strong man, that is, Christ bound the devil. His vessels, these are the hearts of the gentiles. Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? By the viper he shows the synagogue; the brood, these are the Jews; as the son kills the viper its mother, so the Jews [killed] Christ, who is wisdom, the mother of all. An evil and adulterous generation, the same, deserting the Lord, cleaving to idols.

The queen of the South came from the ends of the earth: she signifies the gentiles; to hear the wisdom of Solomon, that is, the teaching of Christ. The unclean spirit goes out from a man, that is, from the Jews; it went through dry places, that is, through the gentiles; it returns to the house, that is, to the Jews; it finds it swept with brooms, that is, [with] the traditions of the fathers; it took with it seven spirits more wicked, these are all their days turned to evil work; entering the house, that is, the hearts of the persecutors, because they persecuted Christ and the prophets. Mother and brothers, that is, the synagogue and the Jews; standing outside, that is, outside the Church; seeking to speak with you, it shows the future conversion of the Jews to faith. Jesus went out of the house; he sat by the sea: this is understood in two ways, that is, from heaven into the world, from the Jews to the gentiles. He went up into a boat, that is, into the heavens; the crowds on the shore, the present life is signified. In a likeness, this is, in parables; he sows who preaches: he sows, that is, the word of God; along the road, that is, one who hears the word of God and does not understand; on rocky ground, that is, one who hears the word of God and received it, and when temptation comes, denies it; among thorns, that is, [one who] hears the word and on account of riches chokes it; in good ground, that is, one who hears and understands. And yields thirtyfold fruit: it shows the order of the married, following the commandment of God; sixtyfold fruit, the order of widows persevering in the Lord; hundredfold fruit, these are the orders of martyrs, monks, or virgins. To him who has it will be given: it shows the apostles; those who have Christ will be given understanding also. And from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away: it shows the Jews; the very Law they had will be taken away from them. Seeing they may not see, these are the Jews, who, seeing with their eyes, did not believe with their heart; hearing they may not hear: it shows the cares of the body; they heard and with hard hearts did not understand. The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field; he who sows is the Son of Man; the seed, the word of God in the hearts of believers; in the field, that is, in the world; the tares, the sons of the wicked one, that is, the workers of iniquity. The enemy who sowed, that is, the devil. The harvest is the end of the age; the reapers are angels. Why is it called a bundle? Because not all are judged alike, but adulterers with adulterers, and all equals equally. The mustard seed signifies Christ; the man sowing is God the Father; in the field, that is, in the world. The least of all seeds: it signifies Christ, rejected by the Jews. But when it has grown, that is, has risen, it becomes a tree, that is, it ascends to heaven; its branches, these are the apostles; the birds in its branches, these are the saints, who despise earthly things and long for heavenly things. Otherwise, the mustard seed, the word of the holy Gospel; the man sowing is Christ; in the field, in the world. The least of all, that is, kept in the hearts of the faithful, on account of the wisdom of the philosophers; it becomes a tree, that is, it rises above all worldly wisdom; its branches show the expositions of the individual teachers; the birds, that is, lovers of knowledge, from the seed received, that is, the teaching of the Gospel.

The woman, that is, wisdom, hid in the meal, that is, in the hearts of the faithful, three measures: it shows the three sons of Noah; until the whole was leavened, that is, until the Gospel was preached in the whole world. The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden: the treasure, that is, Christ or wisdom; in a field, that is, the Church, or in the divine Scriptures. He sold everything, that is, he left behind worthless things, or earthly things; he bought the field, that is, the kingdom of heaven. The merchant, who seeks divine teaching, finds one pearl, that is, the wisdom of Christ; he sold everything, that is, his vices. The kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea: by the dragnet the word of preaching is shown; into the sea, that is, into the world; gathering of every kind of fish, that is, every kind of human being. He hears the word of God beside the shore, that is, near the end of the world; the householder is Christ; the scribes, the teachers, are the apostles. He came into his own country, that is, to the Jews. Tetrarch, that is, from the fourth part of a kingdom.

He bound John and put him in prison: it shows the end of the old Law. Herodias signifies the synagogue; the girl danced at the banquet: it shows the gentiles dancing before idols. The head of John on a dish signifies the body of Christ on the altar, his head in the heart of the faithful; it was given to the girl, that is, to the Church from the gentiles; she brought it to her mother: it shows the conversion of the Jews, in the future. They followed: it shows those on foot; it shows that a man ought to follow God not with former wealth but with his own labour. He healed the sick, that is, he washed [them] of sins and from idols. The hour is already past, that is, the letter of the law; five loaves, that is, the five books of Moses; two fish, that is, the two Testaments, or two orders, that is, of priests and of prophets, or the two books of Joshua. The crowd reclined on the grass, that is, on dry hearts, or reclined on vices. And taking the loaves, looking up to heaven, that is, he drew out the sense; he broke [them], that is, he pressed the history of the law out into the spiritual sense, and the understanding appeared; he blessed, that is, he multiplied. Twelve full baskets, that is, the twelve apostles [filled] with holy teaching. For what reason are women and little children not counted as the men are? Because little children are not able to fight against their vices; and so too women, because theirs is the imperfect sex. He ordered them to get into the boat, that is, into the Church; to go before [him] across the strait, that is, from the Jews to the gentiles. Calling is in four ways: first by nature; second by kinship; third by nation; fourth by affection. A man is spoken of in four ways, [according to] what is said, that is: good [spoken] well: Do penance, and the rest; evil [spoken] evilly: His blood be upon us; good [spoken] evilly, where it is said of the blind man: You alone are his disciple?; evil [spoken] well, where the Apostle says: I have delivered such a man to the destruction of Satan, that the spirit may be saved. When evening had come, he was alone: it shows the end of the world. He alone came to redeem the human race.

The ship in the middle of the sea, that is, the Church in the middle of the world; it was tossed by the waves, that is, it suffered persecutions; a contrary wind, that is, the devil; in the fourth watch of the night Jesus came: it shows in the fourth law, that is, of the Gospel. Jesus walking on the sea, that is, treading down the bitternesses of the world; Peter walked on the waters, on the bitternesses, or treading down the vices of sinners. Peter sinking in the sea, that is, through doubt of faith; so everyone who doubts in faith sinks into sin. Jesus stretched out his hand [and] took hold of him, that is, he gave him the help of faith. These are the four laws: the first in nature; the second the law of the letter; the third of the prophets; the fourth of the evangelists. When he had crossed over, that is, when he had passed across; they came into the land of Gennesaret, that is, from the Jews to the gentiles; they brought to him those who were ill, that is, those serving idols.

The Canaanite woman: she shows the early Church; her daughter troubled by a demon, that is, the Church of the gentiles, corrupted by idols. The girl was healed from that hour: it shows the conversion of the gentiles, from the hour in which they believed in Christ. I was not sent except to the sheep that have perished of the house of Israel: it shows [that he was sent] bodily to the Jews; otherwise, because all who believe in God are called Israel.
