To take the bread, that is, the teaching; of the children, that is, of the Jews; to give to the dogs, that is, to the gentiles. The little dogs eat, that is, the gentiles; they receive of the crumbs, that is, of the lesser commandments.

I have pity on the crowd: it shows that God is wholly merciful; they have stayed with me three days: it shows faith in the Trinity; they have nothing to eat, that is, they do not have the word of preaching; I do not wish to send them away fasting, lest they faint on the way, that is, lest they perish on the way of error in the present life, because faith without works is dead. By the seven loaves he shows the Heptateuch; by the few fish he shows the order of the prophets, or of the priests. Reclining on the ground: it shows that the more perfect have already trodden down their vices; by the seven baskets, the seven teachers of the Holy Spirit. Pharisees, divided; Sadducees, justified. A clear sky, that is, the resurrection of Christ; a red sky, the shedding of blood; a gloomy sky shows the passion of Christ; a glowing storm signifies persecution. Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, that is, of their teaching. Simon, that is, obedient; that is, son of Jonah, that is, dove, which is interpreted the Holy Spirit. Flesh and blood has not revealed [it] to you, that is, father and mother have not shown [it] to you. The gates of hell are the sins of men; the keys of the kingdom of heaven are the power of binding and loosing, that is, they will be opened through penance. To suffer many things from the elders and scribes: saying this, Jesus shows his passion and resurrection. He says to Peter, Get behind me: it shows him crucified. [Whoever comes] after me, let him deny himself, that is, let him despise the pleasure of the flesh. He who loves pleasure loses his own soul: soul here is put for pleasure. He who loses his soul will find it. A man loses his soul in two ways: by martyrdom, and by denial of the body. He will find it, that is, in the kingdom of God. He gives an exchange for his soul who torments his flesh and nourishes his soul.

After six days, now on the seventh: it shows the ages of the world, the seventh of which is understood as rest. Peter, James and John: here he shows the whole Church; he leads them up a mountain, that is, into the kingdom of God. His face shone like the sun, that is, the saints in the glory of the Father; otherwise, the Old Testament shone into the New. His garments white as snow, that is, the gathering of all the faithful. By Moses he shows the letter of the Law; by Elijah, the order of the prophets. Christ with the disciples shows the New Testament. A dark cloud, that is, the letter of the Law. A bright cloud, that is, the preaching of the Gospel. A rain cloud, that is, the preaching of the apostles, who produced the fruit of penance after the ascension of Christ.

When he had come to the crowds, that is, when he had come down into the world. A man fallen on his knees shows the order of the prophets, who prayed for himself as if [for] the Church; his son, a lunatic, shows the people of the gentiles, worshipping idols. He falls into fire, that is, into greed; often into water, that is, into lust.

Pass from here, from the Jews to the gentiles. Go to the sea, that is, to the gentiles. Cast a hook, that is, the word of preaching. The fish that first comes up into the deep shows Cornelius; in its mouth you will find a stater, that is, the confession of faith, the humanity and the divinity. Give it to them for me and for you, that is, for me, faith, and for you, excuse. A little child enters the kingdom of heaven, that is, not small in age but pure in mind: hence the Apostle says, Be little children in malice. Whoever scandalizes one of these, that is, whether by bodily injury or by opposition to faith. Let a millstone be hung, that is, the care or the round of this world; on his neck, in the labour of the world; let him be drowned in the sea, that is, in the world. Your hand, that is, your parent; feet, that is, a servant; eye, that is, your bishop or priest, or teacher and elder. Do not despise one of these, [that is, do not act] against their innocence. The sheep that went astray shows the human race; the shepherd is Christ; the sheep left on the mountains show the orders of angels, who dwell in the heavenly places.

If your brother sins, rebuke him between you and him alone, so that the sin is not exposed and reproach does not arise for the brother; tell the Church, that is, the gathering of the faithful. A heathen, that is, a gentile; and a publican is one who sins publicly. Let not their image be hateful to you, but their works. If two agree, that is, flesh and soul. If the flesh agrees with the soul, he who asks through faith has received.

The kingdom of heaven is like a man, a king, who wished to settle accounts with his servants. The one [who owed] ten thousand talents is the one who sins against God. The one who owed a hundred denarii is the one who sins against his brother; the fellow servants who judged are the angels. When Jesus had finished these sayings, he moved to Galilee, that is, at the end of the world, from the gentiles to Judaea.

A man leaves father and mother: this shows Christ, who leaves the Father in heaven; yet he leaves him in such a way that he does not desert [him]; mother, that is, the synagogue. He will cleave to his wife, that is, Christ to the Church. The two will be in one flesh: this shows that Christ is the head, and the Church truly the body. A wife is deserted by her husband, that is, when someone has departed from Christ, then he joins himself to heresy in one crime. Four souls perish, that is, he who dismisses his wife without reason, and he who marries the dismissed woman. With difficulty will a rich man enter, and the rest: he says this of those who possess under avarice; the eye of the needle is said [to be] a small gate of Jerusalem. In another way, the eye of the needle [is] the confession of faith, or of penance; the rich are said [to be] the Jews; the camel, the people of the gentiles. In a third way, the eye of the needle shows the passion of Christ; the camel, that is, he who carries the sins of the human race. In the regeneration, that is, through the resurrection.

The last will be first, and the first last. The last were the people of the gentiles; the Jews were first, [and] have become last. So [it is] with Peter and the thief; so with the infant and the old man. The householder hired workers into his vineyard: the father is Christ; early in the morning shows the beginning of the world; the workers, those who keep God's commandments; the vineyard, that is, the Church; in the old vineyard, the Law, or the synagogue; the day's denarius, eternal life. In the marketplace, that is, in the world. At the first hour came Abel; at the third hour Noah and his sons; at the sixth hour came Abraham; at the ninth hour came Moses and David; at the eleventh hour came the people of the gentiles. In another way, the first hour, that is, infancy; the second hour, adolescence; the sixth, youth; the ninth, old age; the eleventh, decrepit age. At whatever hour a man, converted, has groaned with his whole heart, he receives the day's denarius. When evening came, that is, at the end of the world. The steward of the vineyard [is] Christ; those who grumbled are the Jews, saying, We have borne the burden of the day, that is, bearing the Law and the prophets.

Jericho is interpreted "moon": it signifies the falling away of the people. The two blind men signify the Jews and the gentiles; sitting beside the road, that is, the present life near its end; Jesus passing by, that is, through the incarnation and humanity he passed through the world; Jesus standing still shows the divinity. When he had drawn near to Jerusalem, that is, when he had come into the world. Bethphage, that is, house of the mouth, or of the jaw; the Mount of Olives, that is, the name of three lights, that is, refreshment from labour, consolation in work, knowledge of the true light. The village that is opposite you, that is, Jerusalem, which fought against the law of the Gospel. Untie and bring [them] to me shows the conversion of the Jews, or of the gentiles, through the preaching of the apostles. The Lord has need, of nothing else but faith; to Zion, that is, watchtower; [say to] the daughter of Zion, that is, the gathering of the faithful; by the garments he shows doctrine; they made him sit on top, that is, Christ in the hearts of the faithful; they spread garments on the road: it shows the conversion of humility. Branches from the trees, that is, the teaching of the gentiles; the crowd that goes before shows the Jews; the crowd following signifies the gentiles. Hosanna, save me, or bring salvation: as you save the Jews, save the gentiles too; as you save the angels, save the human race. Otherwise, branches from the trees, that is, simple teachers, who through simplicity cut off the teaching of the fathers like shoots. Jesus entered the temple, that is, the Church. He threw out the sellers and buyers, that is, those who sell and buy the gifts of the Holy Spirit, who [sell and buy] baptism or any consecration. The chair, that is, teaching; the table, that is, the commandments of the Law; the children crying out in the temple, that is, in the Church. Leaving them, he went outside: it shows the Jews left behind; he went to the gentiles. Bethany, that is, obedient house. There he stayed: it shows that Christ stays in the heart of the obedient; he returns to the city: it shows that in the first coming he came to the Jews. What did he hunger for but the faith of the Jews? The fig tree, that is, the synagogue; beside the road, according to the letter. He found nothing on it but leaves, that is, the substitution of the Jews and of the fathers' teachings. The withered fig tree shows the synagogue without penance. The mountain, that is, Christ. Take [it] away from here, that is, from the Jews; throw [it] into the sea, that is, into the hearts of believers.

A man who had two sons: the man is Christ; the two sons, the Jews and the gentiles. Which of them did the father's will? The one who said, I go, and did not do it, shows the Jews; and the one who said, I will not, and did it, shows the people of the gentiles, who did it through the confession of faith. A householder planted a vineyard: the man is God the Father; the vineyard, the synagogue. He surrounded [it] with a hedge, that is, the guard of the angels. The winepress, that is, the temple, martyrdom; the tower in the middle shows the teaching of the Law; the farmers are the teachers. But when the time of the fruit drew near, that is, the coming of Christ; the servants sent are the prophets; the one they killed first is Jeremiah and Isaiah; the one they stoned is Stephen. They threw him out of the vineyard, that is, Jerusalem, onto the mount of Calvary. The vineyard here, and other tenants, shows the Church of the gentiles, who render fruit, that is, the confession of penance and of faith. The stone, that is, Christ; cut from the mountain without hands, that is, without a man's act and intercourse; from a mother without seed, from the Father without time. Made the head of the corner, it holds together two walls: it shows the New and Old Testament, Jews and gentiles. Whoever falls on the stone will be broken: it signifies the gentiles [falling] upon Christ, from unbelief to faith; will be broken upon, that is, into humility. But on whomever the stone falls, it will crush him: it shows the superstitious Jews.

A man, a king, who made a wedding for his son. The man is God the Father; by the wedding he shows the union of Christ and the Church. As Eve [came] from Adam's rib, so the Church was redeemed from Christ's side; and as Adam came forth from virgin earth, so Christ too was born of the Virgin Mary. He sent his servants, that is, the patriarchs; again he sent others, that is, the prophets. The dinner prepared, that is, Holy Scripture; the bulls slain show those who shed their blood for Christ; the fatlings, that is, fattened [beasts]. They went off to the farm, that is, into greed; others to business, that is, in the world, as the Apostle says: No one serving as a soldier to God entangles himself in worldly business, that he may please him to whom he has proved himself. The rest seized his servants: it shows the onslaught of persecution. He said to his servants, that is, the apostles. The wedding is ready, that is, the hearts of believers joined with Christ through the love of charity. Go to the ends of the roads, that is, to the gentiles. They gathered good and bad: it shows the present life. The king came in to those reclining: it shows the second coming. The man without a wedding garment shows charity, as he says, faith without charity is dead.

The woman, that is, the synagogue; by the seven husbands the Heptateuch is understood. The woman dead, that is, the letter dead, in passing from the Old Testament into the New. In the resurrection whose will she be? That is, the Church's of Christ. The Lord said, that is, God the Father, to my Lord, that is, to Christ: until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet: it shows that through patience he humbled the Jews and gentiles under his feet, so that the persecutors may be punished by vengeance in the future as well. On the chair of Moses, that is, on his teaching; phylacteries, that is, the ten Words of the Law written on a slip, which the Pharisees carried on the forehead.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem: by doubling [the name] he shows the feeling of grief. As a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, with feathers spread, that is, with wings raised, so too Christ spread his palms on the cross to gather his children, as the song of Deuteronomy asserts: He spread his wings, and took them up on his shoulders. Behold, your house will be left to you deserted: it shows that they have been abandoned by their Law, and by prophecy, and by the priesthood. You will not see me until you say, Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord: it shows that in the second coming all flesh will see him, and all the tribes of the earth who pierced him will mourn over themselves. Stone will not be left here upon stone: it shows the dispersion of the Jews. Then many will be scandalized: it shows that through the greatness of the persecution they will deny Christ. The abomination shows the statue of the Antichrist set up in the temple; the desolation, that is, the consummation. Those who are in Judaea, that is, in the confession of faith. Let them flee to the mountains, that is, to the teaching of the apostles; he who is on the roof, that is, in the contemplative life; let him not come down into the house, that is, into the active life; in the field, that is, in the preaching of the Gospel; let him not take his tunic, that is, let him not return to his former way of life.

Woe to those who are pregnant, that is, to those who covet the property of others; and to those who are nursing, that is, who carry it out in deed; by the desert it shows persecution, by the sabbath the end of the world. Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered: the body is Christ; the eagles are the souls of the saints. Otherwise: in the resurrection each soul will take up its own body. By the sun it shows the preaching of the Gospel; by the moon, the Church; by the stars, the saints, or the preachers. The powers of the heavens will be shaken, that is, the hosts of angels [coming] to the judgement; the sign will appear in heaven, that is, the cross of Christ; by the trumpet it shows the sound of the angels. There will be two in the field, that is, in the preaching of the Gospel: one will be taken, that is, he who fulfils the preaching in deed; the other will be left, that is, in works of justice; at the mill, in the world; two grinding, that is, in the Catholic Church and [in that] of the heretics.

The kingdom of heaven is like ten virgins, who took their lamps, that is, in the resurrection, their bodies. They are virgins because they did not deny Christ. Five wise, because they laboured for the kingdom of God; five foolish: it shows those who acted for the reward of human praise. To grow drowsy is to languish before death, but to sleep is to rest in death. At midnight, that is, in error, or negligent in [false] security. I do not know you, that is, I do not know your good works.

The man setting out is Christ; going abroad, that is, from the world to the Father. He called his servants, that is, the teachers; he gave them his goods, that is, the teaching of the Gospel; five talents, that is, the five senses, sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch, which he was accustomed by habit to stir, so that he might turn transitory things toward the eternal. Thus of sight it is said, Turn away my eyes, and the rest. Of hearing, Hedge your ears, and let them not hear tongues of blasphemy. Of smell, We are a good fragrance to God among those who are saved; of taste, Do not curse, but bless; of touch, Let him who used to steal steal no longer, but let him labour with his hands, so that he may give to the needy also. Therefore they become ten talents. Two talents, that is, understanding and action; he who has these, and fulfils them by example and teaches by word, saves himself and instructs others. Therefore the talent is doubled. One talent shows understanding. He hid it in the earth, that is, he who teaches the preaching of the Gospel for earthly things; but after a long time, that is, at the end of the world. He reaps where he did not sow, that is, where there was no preaching; take away the talent, that is, the understanding; give it to him who doubled [it] in good work. The five senses, as the Apostle says: they are a law to themselves, who show the work of the law in their hearts. He who has faith and charity will be given understanding and the working of virtues; he who does not have, even what he has will be taken from him, that is, he who has faith and does not have charity, that very faith will die in him. Majesty, that is, power, dignity. The goats, the Jews; but the sheep, the gentile peoples. Right, that is, prosperous, or upright; left, adverse, or penal, because with God nothing is sinister.

Now when he was in Bethany, that is, in the house of obedience; here the house stands for the world. The woman, that is, the future Church; the alabaster jar, that is, the human body; by the ointment it shows the faith of confession; the head of Christ is God the Father; reclining: likewise Christ over the Church. The poor you will always have, that is, spiritually, those who lack teaching, or bodily, those who lack food. But me you will not always have: it shows [him] according to the flesh. Joseph is sold into Egypt for twenty pieces of silver, so as to satisfy bodily hunger; Christ was sold for thirty pieces of silver, for the sins of men and for the hunger for faith. Opportunity, that is, the fitting time; by the unleavened bread of sincerity it shows sincerity of mind. I will drink it in the kingdom of my Father with you, that is, with his members; in the kingdom, that is, in the Church. I will strike the shepherd, that is, Christ; the sheep will be scattered, that is, the apostles. I will go before you into Galilee: that is, leaving the Jews, he went to the gentiles. If it is possible, let this cup pass from me, that is, the passion: he said this on the part of the flesh; by the sword it shows the divine word. He cut off the ear, that is, the hearing of the Jews cut off; [...] that he might purge uncleanness; scourged, he held firm, so that he might free us from the scourges of sins. As Adam stretched out his hand to the tree of life, so too the Jews stretched out their hands against Christ; accordingly Christ too stretched out his hand on the tree of life; so too the Jews stretched out his hands on the wood of the cross, so that he might free us from every goad. By the cock's crow it shows the refreshment of the Holy Spirit; he was led bound, so that he might loose the bonds of our sins.

Corban in Hebrew, gazophylacium in Greek, is called in Latin the keeping of riches. By the shedding of Christ's blood the human race was redeemed; by the price of blood a field was bought for the burial of strangers. The scapegoat is Barabbas, led into the desert, that is, into hell; the other sacrificed, that is, Christ, for the sin of men. They stripped Christ, that is, despoiled of the faith of the Jews. They clothed [him] in a scarlet cloak, that is, Christ clothed with the faith of the gentiles; otherwise, by the scarlet cloak it shows the shedding of his blood, or martyrdom. They stripped him of the cloak and clothed him in his own garments: it shows the conversion of the Jews at the end of the world.

The soldiers divided his garments among themselves: this bears the figure of the Gospel, [of those] who divided the teaching of Christ among themselves. By the tearing of the veil it shows the tearing of the kingdom of the Jews. In another way, the veil was torn: it shows the tearing of the letter of the Law through the revelation of the Holy Spirit; or, through the ascension of Christ the heavens were torn open to the human race. The earth moved: it shows the grace of God moved from the Jews to the gentiles; the rocks split, that is, the hearts of the gentiles split open to faith; the tombs opened, that is, hearts [opened] to faith.

The tomb, that is, the Church from the gentiles; new: it shows that the word of God had not been preached to the gentiles before; the tomb hewn in the rock shows the Church cut out of the hardness of heathendom; the stone rolled to the door of the tomb shows the hardness in the hearts of the Jews.

The evening of the sabbath, that is, the end of the world; the first [day] of the week shows the day of resurrection; the stone rolled back signifies the hardness of the Jews rolled back in the future; by the lightning it shows terror; by the whiteness of the garment it shows the consolation of correction; in Galilee, on the mountain: it shows [the passage] from the people of the Jews to the gentiles.
ON THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MARK.

The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God: in saying Son of God, it shows the birth according to the divinity; it shows [the birth] according to the flesh when it says Jesus. Behold I send, that is, the voice of the Father; my messenger, that is, John; before your face, that is, the Forerunner of Christ, making him known. The voice is John; the one crying out is Christ. In the desert signifies the Jews, abandoned by the Law, by the kingship, and by the priesthood; prepare the way, that is, hearts, or works; make his paths straight, that is, the thoughts of your heart. By the baptism of water it shows the washing of body and soul; the baptism of penance is the remission of sins. He came into the house of Simon [and] Andrew, that is, to the Jews; rising very early, it shows the coming of Christ and the beginning of the New Testament; he went off to a desert place, that is, to the Jews; and there he prayed, that is, there he preached.

He could not enter the city: this was because of the crowds of people. By the paralytic it shows the human race; by the bed, the body. He was carried by four: these are the four elements of which man consists, or the four orders of the Gospel, or the four virtues of the soul, that is: fortitude, justice, prudence and temperance. Fortitude is to fight against vices; justice is to love God with the whole heart, and one's neighbour as oneself; prudence is to foresee the future; temperance is to put a limit on all anger. They uncovered the roof, that is, laying open the history of the Law; they let down the pallet: it shows the letter of the Law laid bare, the sense of the Gospel made plain.

He instructed them to serve him in a boat, that is, to preach in the Church. He went up the mountain: it signifies his ascension with the flesh into heaven; the thunderer is Christ; the sons of thunder are the apostles; the clouds, the prophets; the rain is preaching. A lamp under a bushel, that is, he who teaches out of worldly greed; under a bed, that is, in the obscurity of offenders. Nothing is hidden that will not be made manifest: the hidden law of the Jews, which has been made manifest to the gentiles. The man who sowed shows the teacher; what he sowed, that is, the divine word; in the earth, in the heart of men; sleeping, that is, not knowing; by the night it shows adversity, or ignorance; but by the day it shows prosperity, or knowledge; by the shoot, compunction of heart; by the blade, the faith of works; by the ear, the perfection of action; the full grain in the ear shows the completion of works; by the sickle, the cutting off of the present life and the consummation of the age.

Dismissing the crowd of the Jews, he went off into the boat, that is, into the Church from the gentiles. Other boats were with him, that is, the various churches of the heretics. By the storm of wind it shows the persecutions against the faithful; it was sending waves so that the boat was filling: it shows the persecution of Antichrist, which will be most savage, so that many will come close to denial; those loved by God persevere in the faith. Christ sleeping in the stern shows the testing of the faithful in persecution. They wake him, that is, they call upon him in persecution, to help them. There was a great calm, that is, after the persecution of Antichrist, and after the resurrection. The man having an unclean spirit signifies the human race; breaking his chains shows the gentiles transgressing the law of their nature, or the teaching of the philosophers. So also the Jews, breaking the letter of the Law, or prophecy. He cut himself with stones: it shows the gentile people worshipping stones.

The man sitting, clothed, at faith in Jesus, shows [one] clothed with faith and charity; in his right mind, that is, with a pure and sincere mind. She had spent her substance on physicians, that is, because she had placed all her faith, and her way of life and her hope, in philosophers. He sent them two by two: it shows the two Testaments, so that they should preach the same things everywhere; likewise also because charity does not exist in fewer than two. By the staff it shows consolation, or discipline, as Paul says: What do you wish? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in the spirit of gentleness and consolation? Shod with sandals, for three reasons: because of thorns, that is, for the bond of riches, or the anxiety of the world; because of cold, that is, for greed of mind or unbelief; because of serpents, that is, because of the teaching of heretics. Not with two tunics, that is, not with a double mind, nor with wavering between faith and unbelief, not with a double trust, in the New or in the Old. Not like the hypocrites, who seek praise from men. By the supper which no meal follows, the consummation of the age, which saw its consummation when Christ came. The hour has already passed, that is, the letter of the Law; hence he says: The old things have passed away, and behold, new things have been made.

The boats in the midst of the sea, that is, the Church in the tossing of the world. Jesus alone on the sea signifies that he alone was born on earth without [human] touch; the contrary wind shows the persecution of the devil against the apostles after Christ's ascension. He wished to pass by them: it shows [this was] to test them. Gennesaret is interpreted 'fitting harbour'. He went into the regions of Tyre and Sidon, that is, to the gentiles; entering into a house, that is, into the world.

He wished no one to know: it shows humility. He could not be hidden, that is, because his works are always manifest. By the woman is understood the early Church. She fell down before the feet of Jesus: these are the apostles. Let the children first be fed, that is, the Jews, so that they may receive the commands of the law of the Gospel; and if they judge [themselves] unworthy of the kingdom of God, then let the gentiles receive it. She found the girl lying on the bed, that is, she found her in the former [state] of her body. By the deaf and dumb man it shows the human race; he was deaf who did not hear the commands of God; and dumb, he could not speak, because he could not render the confession of praise, and did not have the confession of faith. He leads him out of the crowd: it shows a withdrawn life, because in withdrawal a man always recognises the blindness of his sins, [and returns] to the former way of life of a good nature. He put his fingers into the ears of his heart, and opened his mouth in the confession of faith. Looking up to heaven: it shows that all should render praise to God; he groaned, that is, for the sins of the human race, which stood out in the world. Otherwise: to give us an example, that we should ask God with supplications.

By the blind man it shows the human race; those who brought him to Jesus show the teachers. Taking his hand, that is, he gave [him] the power to act. He led him out of the village: it shows withdrawal into the contemplative life, or out of the former way of life. Spitting on his eyes: by the spittle it shows the incarnation of Christ, by which the human race has been enlightened; laying on his hands, that is, he gave the help of action.

I see men as if trees: here it shows an example of humility, that no one should be puffed up about his virtues, but should consider himself less and lower than all. Again he laid his hands on his eyes, and they were opened: it shows that he opened the hearts of men, so that they might see the knowledge of God clearly, and believe without doubt; he was restored, that is, in good works.

He sent him into his house, that is, he recalled him to the former [state] of worldly nature. Christ's descent from the mountain shows his descent from the heavens. Here the disciples hold the rank of the prophets or patriarchs. The crowds questioning them: it shows the coming of Christ, in that the crowds sought the law from the prophets and patriarchs. They will greet him: here it understands greeting as [a sign of] humility. He who brought his son holds the rank of the patriarchs; the son shows the human race; by the foam it shows pride; by the gnashing of teeth [...]; by withering, it shows avarice. The disciples could not cure [him]: here the disciples bear the figure of the patriarchs, because neither prophets nor patriarchs could cure the human race, until Christ came and redeemed it with his blood, as the prophet says: A brother does not redeem, that is, Moses through the Law; a man redeems, that is, Christ. From infancy, that is, from the first age of the human race. The father of the child said: I believe, help my unbelief: it shows that he said, if faith is lacking, increase it. Tearing him greatly: it shows that when the devil saw he was about to be driven from the earth at the end of the world, then power is given him to do as much as he wishes, on account of God's elect; when he saw himself being expelled from each man through confession and penance, then he stirred up vices and the cruellest assaults against them all the more. He became as if dead: here it shows an example: the purified man, that is, one who mortifies himself through confession and penance. Here Jesus seems to have performed two miracles: he cured [him] of the demon, and raised one as if dead; so he raised the human race from the death of sins, and freed it from the demon of servitude. By the millstone the circuit of the world is shown; by the ass, the uncleanness of sins.

To be sunk in the sea, that is, to humble oneself in the world through penance, or to perish in one's own sin: because it is lighter to bear punishment for oneself alone than to drive others too away from the kingdom of God. By the worms it shows those who repent late; it always gnaws him in punishment, because while he had time he did not amend. Everyone will be salted with fire: by the fire is understood the kindling of the Holy Spirit, because just as all flesh perishes without salt, so every man without knowledge of the word of God becomes foolish. Have salt in yourselves, that is, have the wisdom of God in yourselves. They come into the borders of Judaea: it shows that the Jews will in the future return to the faith of Christ.

Beyond the Jordan, that is, to the grace of baptism. Let the little children come to me: here the little children bear the figure of the gentiles; the disciples who forbade [them] bear the figure of the Jews. Camels cannot pass through the eye of a needle unless their loads are laid down; so also the Jews, unless the load of sins, or riches, is laid down, cannot enter the kingdom of God. What did Peter leave, who said: We have left all things? It shows that a man leaves much who puts himself last. Let him go before them, that is, let him go before his sheep by examples. By the cup it shows the passion; by the baptism, the mortification, or falling asleep, of the Church. Just as Adam sinned through three things, that is, he coveted, he transgressed, he acted proudly, so also Christ was three days in the tomb; likewise and accordingly a man is plunged three times under the water of baptism; hence the Apostle says: For we are buried with Christ through baptism; for we have been baptised into his death. Whoever wishes to be first among you will be the servant of all: here it shows the teachers of the Church. The blind man bears the figure of the gentiles. He was sitting beside the way, that is, beside the faith.

He cried out to Jesus: Have mercy on me. The moral sense: when we apply ourselves to prayer, then the crowd, phantasms, rebuke the minds of the faithful to be silent, since they wish to shut us out from prayer while we persevere. Then Jesus stands beside us: for to stand belongs to the divinity, but to pass by belongs to the humanity. He commanded them to be called, that is, through the preaching of the apostles he calls the gentiles to faith. He threw off his garments, that is, his former way of life; leaping up, that is, from ignorance to knowledge, from unbelief to faith. You will find a colt tied: it shows the gentiles tied with the guilt of sins; on which no one has sat, that is, where no teacher has preached. Untie it and bring it to me, that is, bring [them] to faith through preaching.

He saw a fig tree: it shows that the faith of the Jews was far from Christ. It was not the season for figs, that is, it was not the time for the Jews to believe, because they judged themselves unworthy of the kingdom. He did not allow [anyone] to carry a vessel through the temple, that is, the hearts of the faithful: Christ does not wish any other work to be done, or to pass through, except what is holy. To hand it over to tenants, that is, to keep the Law. The winepress: this is the temple of Solomon; otherwise it shows martyrdom. He came to the synagogue: the hedge for the synagogue is the guard of angels; the tower, this is the Law. They threw him out of the vineyard, that is, from the Jews to the gentiles. Otherwise: from the city of Jerusalem to Mount Calvary.

The widow put in two coins, that is, a farthing, by which he means the 'four-square' man who has offered himself to God. Whatever you ask, believing in prayer, will be done for you: how then does Saint Paul say: Three times I asked the Lord about the goad, and it did not depart from me? The devil asked to tempt Job, and God permitted him. Paul was not heard, so that through that very goad he might be crowned; the devil was heard, so that through his temptations Job might be crowned. Accordingly the Apostle says: We do not know what we should ask, except [through] Christ, who intercedes for us. Nation against nation, that is, [the nation] of pagans against [that] of Christians. Morally: the flesh against the soul; the kingdom of the devil against the kingdom of Christ; the vices of the flesh against the spirit of good work. Earthquakes, that is, from unbelief to faith, that is, the body or the soul, [moved] to hear the word of God. Standing for my sake as a testimony to them, that is, if they believe your testimony, it will be for them unto life; and if they do not believe, it will be for them unto punishment.

Of the day and hour no one knows except the Father: it shows [this] on behalf of the body, because the Church is the body of Christ. As for his saying, you do not know the time, that is, the end of each person, or the consummation of the age.

A man went away on a journey, that is, Christ [went] from the world with the flesh to heaven; he left his house, that is, the Church; to the teachers of each work, that is, of each grace of virtue; by the doorkeeper he shows the bishop, or the teacher. In the evening fire and sulphur rained from heaven on Sodom; at midnight Egypt was struck in its firstborn; in the morning Sodom was overthrown, and its ash went up to heaven. Lest he come suddenly and find you sleeping, that is, in ignorance, or in the security of negligence.

She broke the alabaster jar: it signifies the body of Christ, wounded on the cross; by the ointment the confession of faith is shown; the head of Christ is God the Father. He sought an opportune [time] to betray him: it shows that the time had opportunely come for the ruin of the Jews, or of Judaea, and the opportunity of the redemption of the Church. On the first day of unleavened bread, that is, on Thursday; the Church was made the unleavened bread of sincerity. Passover ('passing over') is spoken of in four ways, that is, from the world to the Father, from the Jews to the gentiles, and we from unbelief to faith, from death to life.

A man carrying a jar of water bears the figure of the apostles, or of their successors and of the baptisers, through whom baptism is performed; the jar signifies the baptism of the Trinity. To eat the Passover with his disciples: it shows himself with the disciples [sent] to the Jews; otherwise, he eats in his members, which is the Church. By the upper room the higher way is shown; by the large furnished [room] the breadth of the Church is shown. The lamb sacrificed in Egypt shows the mystery of the body and blood sacrificed in the New Testament; because the old sacrifice of the Jews has departed, that is, the blood of goats and bulls; now our sacrifice, which is called [that] of wine, was offered by Melchizedek when Abraham was returning from the slaughter. That they asked one by one shows that no one should be confident of his own conscience. Leaving the linen cloth, he fled from them naked: it shows the malice of the Jews left behind; he fled naked: it shows that the apostles, stripped of the superstitions of the Jews, went away to the gentiles. Peter was warming himself at the fire: it signifies the lukewarmness of the apostles, and his own denial, and the unbelief of the Jews.

They will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of power: it shows that Stephen saw him; Saul also saw [him] when he was struck down on the road; and many others saw [him]. Pilate is interpreted 'mouth of the hammerer': he who shapes is not shaped; so too persecutors shape the souls of the just for the kingdom of heaven, while they themselves have remained unshaped by the grace of God. The Lord took the crown of thorns upon himself to wash away the thorns of our sins; hence it was said to Adam: Thorns and thistles shall spring up for you. As for its saying that Jesus was crucified at the third hour, it shows that he was judged to be crucified; at the sixth hour he was raised up on the cross. Eli, Eli lamma sabactani, that is, God, my God, why have you forsaken me: it shows that he was forsaken in respect of the flesh, not according to the divinity, because there is a unity of power. He left the flesh of the Son for an hour in the passion, so that through his own Son he might have adopted sons. As the sponge was full of vinegar in its hollows, so too the Jews were full of superstitions and bitter doctrine. Joseph bears the figure of the early Church from the gentiles. He bought a linen cloth: by the price of the linen cloth it shows the confession of faith; by the linen cloth it shows the mortification of the Church, or the grace of the baptised; the body of Jesus wrapped in a new linen cloth, that is, Christ encompassed by the Church, and the recalling of regeneration; by the tomb and the linen cloth it shows the altar on which the body of Christ is placed. Otherwise, the Church, those who have received Christ through faith in their hearts; or the eating of his body and the taking of his blood. The rock is Christ.

The tomb hewn from rock shows the Church built from the side of Christ. He rolled a stone to the door of the tomb: it shows Christ hidden in the law and prophecy; by the stone rolled away it shows the history of the law laid open, Christ in the New Testament. He is not here, that is, he is not among the Jews, but among the gentiles. Go, tell his disciples and Peter: he names [him] because of the denial, so that he would not despair, and because of the primacy of the apostleship.

Mary, from whom he had cast out seven demons. By the seven demons it shows her whole life defiled, because [life] revolves through seven days. Preach the Gospel to every creature, that is, to every man: because man has a share with the rest of creation: with the angels, understanding or discerning; with the beasts, seeing and feeling; with the trees, living: wood lives by its greenness, and so does man through youth; with the stones, being, because men who believe are like stones.

They will cast out demons: whether spiritually or bodily. They will speak with new tongues, or with diverse tongues; the new tongue is the preaching of the Gospel. They will take up serpents, that is, serpents' venom, or the doctrine of heretics; if they drink anything deadly it will not harm them, nor will the doctrine of heretics. [They will lay] hands on the sick, that is, whether [sick] of body or of soul. We read of three taken up with the body from the world into heaven: the Lord was raised by his own power, because he was neither begotten through intercourse nor begetting through intercourse, but was born of a virgin; Enoch was taken away, because [he was] begetting through intercourse; Elijah was snatched up with a chariot, because he was begotten through intercourse, not begetting through intercourse, because he remained a virgin.
ON THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE.

Luke, rising up himself, a Syrian of Antioch by nation, a physician by profession, a disciple of the apostles, followed Paul, serving God without reproach, never having a wife; he died at the age of eighty-three in Bithynia, full of the Holy Spirit, and was buried in Constantinople. He wrote the Gospel in Achaia in the Greek language. Matthew wrote for the believing Jews, Mark for penitents, John for the perfect, Luke for the believing Greeks.

There was in the days of Herod, and the rest. Here he has completed the order: he has named the king and the region in which he was, the priest and his people, and he indicates his wife. Of the division of Abijah, that is, in the days of the Lord. Zechariah is interpreted 'mindful of the Lord'; the angel of the Lord appeared to him at the right of the altar: it shows that the mystery of God is shown to him because he is mindful of the Lord. Abijah is interpreted 'father of the Lord': it was fitting that he who would preach the Father as Lord should be conceived at the time of the office of 'the father of the Lord'. Elizabeth is interpreted 'fullness of my God': she bears the figure of Mary, who was full of God. And both were just before the Lord, not before men, because formerly a barren woman was accursed under the law. Walking in all the commandments, that is, they kept the whole law.

They had no son, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days. These two circumstances are mentioned so that the miracle would have been a greater testimony. Zechariah entered the temple, that is, Christ [entered] into Mary. The people pray, that is, the people first ask Zechariah, that is, for freedom from captivity. An angel appeared to him: it did not say 'came', because he was there before. Zechariah was troubled, that is, because the Jews will be troubled at the coming of Christ. Your prayer has been heard, that is, more than you asked: you asked for the liberation of the people, and the Forerunner has been given to you. And many will rejoice at his birth, because after ruin they will rejoice unto eternal life.

Because he himself said, Behold the Lamb of God, and the rest: he goes before Christ: he was baptised before, and preached before, was conceived before, born before, and died before: six circumstances, because there were six months between them. I am Gabriel, that is, the strength of God. Elizabeth conceived: it did not say of Zechariah, he knew his wife, because the will of desire had failed in them. And she hid herself, for modesty, so as to test whether what she had conceived was true; for five months, that is, the five thousand [years] of the world, or the five books of Moses.

Take away my reproach, that is, the reproach of barrenness, and of conception in old age; among men, because it was no reproach before God. Just as in the sixth month Gabriel was sent by the Lord to a city, so in the sixth millennium of the world Christ was sent. Joseph is interpreted 'saviour', [like the one] who saved Egypt from famine. Or: Mary blessed, that is, by the flesh of Christ. But she was troubled because she did not know whether what the angel said concerned the past or the future. The Holy Spirit will come upon you: 'Spirit' is the name of every grace when it is breathed in; [this is] how Mary recognised what the angel said, or, since she was full of the Spirit, she knew that the angel had spoken to her. The power of the Most High will overshadow you, that is, it hid him in Egypt by flight. Your kinswoman: she is called this because Elizabeth was of the tribe of Levi, that is, of the tribe of God. Behold the handmaid of the Lord, as it says, the son of your handmaid.

He went into the hill country with haste: because everyone [who would] fulfil the will of God ought to make haste. The infant leapt in his mother's womb, that is, the son honoured the son, just as the woman honoured the woman. She cried out with a loud voice. It was fitting, because of John it was said, the voice of one crying in the wilderness. John is his name: why did he not say 'John will be'? Because he was named by the angel before he was conceived. And they marvelled, that is, at the agreement between father and mother. Blessed be our Lord: the goodness of God, [shown] when Zechariah prayed for the liberation of the people and the Forerunner was given to him. He has raised up a horn of salvation, that is, Christ, because a horn is neither flesh nor bone; so too Christ is neither bone nor flesh: only divinity. The boy grew, that is, in body. This first enrolment was made, that is, among the Romans, because Julius first reigned over the Romans, but did not hold the whole world; and after him Augustus reigned, after Augustus Tiberius. In the time of Augustus and Tiberius the time of Christ is completed, his baptism: because in the fifteenth year of the reign of Augustus, Augustus and his son Tiberius came in one chariot to their city. After they had [...] the lamb of the world, it shows that in his reign would be born the one who would reign in the whole world, and the father [showed] the unity of his son's will. At that very time a circle of bronze appeared around the sun: it shows that in his time was born the one whose power and beauty and light and wisdom would have encompassed all power: the first beauty, light and wisdom. At that very time a spring of oil flowed from the taberna meritoria the whole day until evening: it shows that in his time was born the one from whom the spring of oil would have flowed, that is, the spiritual anointing through the whole Gospel to the end of the world. Augustus figures the Father, Tiberius the Son. The census is given for this reason, so that the king might know the number and the greatness of the people. By the governor of Syria: it shows the place from which Christ came. That each should register in his own city: it shows that no one outside the Church renders tribute to God. Laid in a manger, that is, the body of Christ upon the altar. The ox and the ass at the manger of Christ show the Gentiles and the Jews communicating upon the altar. A place in the inn, that is, a house between two walls has two doors: the figure of the Church, between paradise and the world. The host of soldiers shows [them] following Christ as leader. The shepherds spoke: it was fitting that shepherds should speak; it was fitting that shepherds should give testimony about the true lamb. Let us go over to Bethlehem: it shows us not to look back, nor to the right, nor to the left, but to Christ. They found Mary, Joseph and the infant: through these three the world was healed.

Mary kept all these words, that is, what the angel said to her. After eight days were completed, that he should be circumcised: and in the eighth beatitude it shows the passion of Christ, when it is said, Blessed are those who suffer persecution. The circumcision of Christ on the eighth day shows the blood of the martyrs up to the day of judgement; or because he fulfilled the law and did not abolish it. After the days of her purification were fulfilled, that is, twelve days for a boy, thirty for a girl were [set] in the Law, during which a woman should not enter the church. A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons: through the fierceness of the turtledove it shows prudence like that of the serpent, through the dove that we are simple; 'a pair' shows that a man should offer his whole self to God. A revelation to the Gentiles, that is, the glory of faith. Behold, he is set for the fall, that is, for those who do not believe; for the rising, for those who believe in him; and a sign, that is, the Gospel. I came to set a man against his mother, and the rest: as he himself says, Who is my mother? Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the rest: that is, so that many may think good thoughts, since Mary is not the only mother of Christ.

And a sword will pierce through your own soul, that is, the word of God, or the passion of Christ. She had lived with her husband seven years, that is, the synagogue with the Heptateuch. And she did not depart from the temple, that is, because the Church ought not to depart from heaven. And the boy grew, that is, in body. And he was strengthened, that is, in spirit. When he was twelve years old, that is, the twelve tribes which came to Christ. After three days they found him: the father, that is, the Church, and the mother, that is, the synagogue, who sought him through three Laws, and did not find him except through the Gospel. And he was subject to them: it shows that the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve.

From the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar: at the birth of Christ the first king and first governor are mentioned, that is, when they had not yet begun to teach; but now the king [and] the fourth tetrarch are mentioned, when he came to preaching and to baptism. The king signifies Christ, and the four tetrarchs show the four Gospels; the two priests, that is, the two laws; through the number six the world was made. The first king, of the Romans, shows the unity of the kingdom of the Romans, and the fourth tetrarch over the Jews shows the division of the kingdom of the Jews. The word of the Lord came upon John: go and preach baptism. Every valley shall be filled, that is, Jews and Gentiles; mountains and hills shall be brought low, that is, he who humbles himself is exalted; and the crooked shall become straight, that is, he who was lustful, let him be chaste; and the rough [shall become] level ways, that is, he who is proud, let him be humble. All flesh shall see the salvation of God, that is, Jews and Gentiles, men and women. He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: it shows that a man should not forget the Church in which he was nurtured. And he stood up to read: here it shows that if something has been revealed to a younger man, the elder should be silent, that is, the Evangelist and the Pentateuch; Peter too rises in the midst of the disciples. He stood: it shows that [the word] is to be preached, not [merely] rendered. Because he has anointed me, that is, not with common oil, but spiritual; to preach the gospel to the poor, that is, as: blessed are the poor in spirit; and redemption to captives, that is, to the Jews from Pharaoh and to the Gentiles from the devil; sight to the blind, that is, to Jews and Gentiles; to set free the broken, that is, the Jews by making clay [bricks], and the Gentiles by praying to idols; the year of the Lord, that is, because a year has four seasons, it shows the four evangelists; and the twelve months show the twelve apostles; and the day of retribution, that is, the day of judgement. Literally: today this Scripture is fulfilled in your ears.

There were many widows in Israel, that is, the Church; Elijah signifies Christ; Naaman the Syrian signifies the Gentiles; the daughter, that is, the synagogue; Gehazi, that is, the Church. Having a demon, that is, by believing in idols. What have we to do with you? that is, torments for us, glory for you. Beside the lake, that is, beside the law. Two boats, that is, two Churches. Put out into the deep, that is, Christ ascending into heaven. Labouring all day we have caught nothing, that is, through the old Law we have led no one to life. They filled both boats, that is, because he converted through the Church and the synagogue. So that they were sinking, that is, a man who cannot bear riches and poverty. Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinner: it shows, that is, the Lord did not depart, because he does not forsake true humility.

Do not be afraid, that is, let the sinner not fear the physician. The report about him spread all the more, that is, of healing and teaching. When he prayed, it shows the contemplative life; when he sat, it shows the active life. Through the tiles, that is, through the divinity. Rise and walk: it shows the resurrection of all. He went out onto the mountain to pray, and came down to the crowds: it shows the contemplative and the active [life] in one.

Four beatitudes are read [here], because the four cardinal virtues are contained [in them]. 'Cardinal' is said in Latin [as if] 'of the heart'. These four [...] show the four parts of the world. Likewise eight pertains to the eight souls who were in Noah's ark, through whom it shows the whole human race. Your reward is great in glory, that is, for preaching, persecution and patience. So their fathers did to the prophets, that is, they hated, reproached and cast out their names. Woe to you who are rich, for you have your consolation, and you do not give thanks to God: not to God, but to your riches. Woe to you when men bless [you], that is, your enemies. Hoping for nothing from it: give what you have, so that in glory you may receive a reward from the Lord.

Can the blind lead the blind? that is, can a fool teach a fool? Both will fall into the pit, that is, into perdition. He went into a city called Nain: it shows that after healing the sick man he raised a dead one, because sickness precedes death. The only son of his mother, that is, Adam, from the earth, is carried by four, that is, by the four elements of which man is made. The bier is touched by God, that is, the wood of the cross, because Adam perished through wood. A man is carried by earth when he thinks only of earthly things, or when he is sick and cannot walk; he is carried by water when he thinks of indulging in lust, or when through excessive cold his body cannot be touched; he is carried by air when he does everything for human praise, or when through sickness he cannot [...]; he is carried by fire when through excessive fever he cannot be touched. The Lord raised three dead, that is, the only son of his mother, and the ruler's daughter, and Lazarus: the first in the house, that is, in thought; the second at the gate, that is, in word; the third from the tomb, that is, in deed. He who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he, that is, Christ, because the angels [...]; as it says: you made him a little less than the angels; yet Christ is greater than John, reigning with the Father. Wisdom is justified by her children, that is, the people and the publicans justified God.

An alabaster [jar] of ointment, that is, the body with faith. Standing behind, after the Lord's ascension. At the feet, that is, of the apostles. She wet them with tears, that is, inward charity toward God. With her hair, that is, to give superfluous food and clothing. She kissed his feet, that is, to have peace with all. One owed five hundred denarii, that is, the sins of the Gentiles committed through the five senses; the other fifty, that is, the sins of the Jews. This woman was Mary Magdalene, from whom seven demons were cast out. Who is this who forgives sins? that is, divine power and might. This Mary figures the Church, from which he cast out seven vices, because man sinned in seven days. A certain man, that is, the people of the Gentiles; for a long time, that is, from the beginning of the world; he wore no clothing, that is, faith; nor did he stay in a house, that is, in the Church; but in the tombs, that is, the habit of sinning; with chains and fetters, that is, the law of nature and of the letter. Sitting, that is, in faith, after baptism; clothed, that is, in immortality; at his feet, that is, at the apostles'. He sent him away and said, Return to your house: it shows that we come from the contemplative to the active [life].

The woman, that is, the Church; a flow of blood, that is, the law of nature; for twelve years, that is, two ages. She touches the fringe of his garment, that is, she believed in the least commandment of Christ. Who is it that touched me? that is, who believed in me. Power has gone out from me, that is, to prove who had faith. Peter and John and James, that is, faith, hope, charity; the father, that is, the bishop; the mother, the Church; villages and cities, that is, servants and masters. They told him what they had done. The day began to decline, that is, night was coming. Send the crowd away, the Jews. You give them to eat, that is, preach to the Gentiles. He blessed, that is, the Gospel; he broke, that is, literally. The Son of man must suffer many things, that is, die: [as] sailors [...] from the danger of the voyage, who after the danger saw calm; his departure: to suffer many things.

On the next day, that is, under the second law. A man from the crowd cried out, that is, Abraham; an only son, that is, the whole race; suddenly crying out, that is, being angry; and dashes him down, in flattery of his neighbour; it tears him, that is, in despair; with foam, that is, with folly. A hand on the plough, that is, work upon the Gospel; back, that is, to the world; the ploughshares, that is, charity; four oxen, that is, the four evangelists. The Lord appointed seventy other disciples, as Moses chose seventy elders from the twelve tribes, that is, so that he might unite by humility into one language the seventy languages which had been divided through pride. Two by two: the animals in the ark, and two disciples for preaching, charity; it shows the New and Old Testament; body and soul, man and woman, and two disciples.

I send you as lambs among wolves: I am the shepherd, you are the sheep; the wolves, that is, the scribes and Pharisees. The demons are subject to us, that is, what was not in the Law [is] in the mouth. Over serpents, that is, over heathens, because a serpent does not kill [outright], but pours out the venom of [its] teaching; and scorpions, whose tail and head kill alike: so the devil, who wishes to deceive at the beginning and at the end. A man was going down, that is, the world, which is called accursed; among robbers, that is, demons; they stripped him, that is, of good faith; they beat him, that is, made him sin; they left him half alive, that is, the body alive, the conscience and soul dead. The priest, that is, Aaron; the Levite, that is, the tribe of Levi with its law; the Samaritan, that is, Christ, who is from the outskirts of Samaria; it is interpreted 'guardian', because of Christ, the Lord guarding the little ones. He bound up his wounds, that is, through penance he bound up sins; he poured in oil and wine, the severity and gentleness of Scripture, reward and punishment; onto his own beast, that is, into his own body, because through the passion he brought the human race to the inn, that is, to the Church; two denarii, that is, he gave two laws to the innkeeper, that is, the order of teachers; whatever more you spend, that is, whatever you do by your diligence in teaching men; I, on returning, that is, at the judgement, will repay you.

Martha, that is, the active Church. Mary, that is, the contemplative Church, which always hears Christ's words. Martha said that her sister should help her, because the active life has need of being helped by the contemplative. A friend, that is, a teacher; at midnight, that is, at an inopportune time; three loaves: it shows faith in the Trinity. My friend, that is, another doing penance; from a journey, that is, from the world; I have nothing to set before him, that is, I do not know how to teach him; the door shut, that is, the door of heaven, which nothing opens but charity; my children are with me, that is, the heavenly powers. What is outside and inside, that is, he who made the body also made the soul. Give alms, and all things are clean; and if you do not give, all that you have is unclean.

Do not be afraid, little flock: these are the Jews, because they believed that whoever became poor was cursed in the law. Your loins girded: it shows chastity; lamps burning, that is, good works; so that when he comes, that is, in pain; and knocks, that is, the soul through death; they may open at once, that is, to be always ready; passing by he will serve them, that is, eternal life after the judgement. I came to cast fire on the earth, that is, charity. And those eighteen Galileans signify those on whom the tower fell, that is, the Holy Spirit, because Siloam means 'sent'. Leave it this year too, that is, the Gospel; I will dig around it, that is, let me preach; a basket of dung, to confess sins; in the future, that is, at the day of judgement. The woman, that is, the human race; with a spirit of infirmity, that is, in faith and work; eighteen years, that is, the two laws, or those who did not fulfil the ten words of the law and did not believe in the resurrection, because it happens on the eighth day; by three sixes it shows that she was infirm before the law, under the law, under grace. Bent toward the earth, that is, earthly desires; to look up, that is, because she did not seek heavenly things through penance; he called her to him, that is, through confession; and laid his hand on her, that is, good examples; she was healed, the hope of health; on the first [day] of the sabbath, that is, into the rest to come. Tell that fox, that is, Herod, because [as] the fox is an animal that dwells within and destroys the vineyard, so Herod, the devil, destroys the vineyard, as it is said: you brought a vine out of Egypt.

The man with dropsy, that is, the human race, commits fornication; he took hold of him and healed him: it shows that then the onrush of fornication is healed. A man, that is, God the Father; a great supper, that is, the Gospel; he called many, that is, the Jews; he sent his servant, that is, Christ in the flesh; all things are ready, that is, what was prophesied of Christ. I have bought a farm, that is, because of avarice I did not come to Christ; yokes of oxen, that is, pride; otherwise, yokes of oxen, the five senses, or the five books of Moses; I have married a wife, that is, lust. The poor and the feeble, that is, those who recognise their sins; go out into the roads, that is, to the gentiles; compel them to come in, that is, through confession. To build a tower, that is, to follow Christ; the cost, that is, to renounce the world. What king, that is, the apostle(s); to wage war, that is, the weighing of works; against another king, that is, against Christ; with ten thousand, that is, with the works which a man perceives; with twenty thousand, that is, with the works which are in secret and in the open; he sends an embassy, that is, by showing mercy, by giving alms; he asks for terms of peace, that is: Do not enter into judgement with your servant, Lord. On the earth, that is, into riches; on the dunghill, that is, into poverty. A certain woman, that is, riches; a lighted lamp, that is, the Gospel; the drachma found in the house, that is, a sinner converted in the Church.

A certain man, that is, God the Father. Two sons, the Jews and the gentiles, because the law was given to the Jews first; give me my portion, that is, the present life; he divided his substance, that is, he gave freedom of choice to both peoples. He set out abroad, that is, away from God; by living riotously, that is, by worshipping idols; a severe famine, that is, of the word of God; to one of the citizens, that is, to a philosopher; on his farm, that is, in the world; to feed swine, that is, he lived after the manner of swine; and with the husks, that is, to fill the belly and not grow fat; the swine, that is, the foolish. My father's hired servants, that is, those who are the lowlier servants of God, are filled with bread, that is, with doctrine. I have sinned against heaven: those say this who have the devil for father, who sinned in heaven. Moved with mercy, that is, he came in the flesh; to his servants, that is, to the apostles; the best robe, faith, which Adam lost; a ring, that is, the cross on the forehead; shoes, that is, the Gospel; the fatted calf, that is, Christ out of the two laws. He was dead, that is, Adam; he has come to life again, that is, through baptism; he was lost, that is, in despair; he is found, that is, in hope. The elder son, that is, the Jews; in the field, that is, in unclean desire; music and dancing, that is, prophecy and the Gospel; two servants, that is, Isaiah, etc.

Lazarus the beggar: it gives the name of the poor man, and not of the rich man; good men are written in heaven, and the wicked are not. Full of sores, that is, of sins; the rich man signifies the Jews; the poor man, the gentiles; the dogs, the teachers, who heal wounds with the tongue. In Abraham's bosom, that is, in rest; buried in hell, that is, in the letter; lifting up his eyes, because the Jews were eyes, that is, good in living until Christ; he saw Abraham: so it will be after the judgement from hell; they will see the kingdom of God, so that they may have greater punishment from the greater joy. The tip of his finger in water, that is, those who give small alms; I am tormented in this flame, that is, his own punishment; a great chasm, that is, the confusion of all things, or the old Law. You received good things in your life, that is, you did good, you received [your reward]; Lazarus evil things, that is, because he did not receive punishment for his evils in his life. Five brothers, that is, the five books of Moses, they kept watch for a sign; if one rises from the dead, that happened when Christ rose: some of the Jews believed. If a millstone, that is, if the gentiles [...]; as a horse turning a mill does not see whom it serves, so the philosopher teaches philosophy, which does not profit him, but profits holy Church. Increase our faith, that is, while you increase the commandment.

To this mulberry tree, that is, to the Gospel, which proclaims the red cross of Christ, just as the mulberry is red; to be uprooted, that is, from the Jewish people; and to be planted, among the gentile people. That is, the mulberry tree: its fruit is first white, afterwards red, then black; so the devil, while he was an angel, was white; black at the occasion of Adam; red in the murder of Abel by Cain. Two grinding: it shows two Churches, or two Testaments. The judge and the widow, concerning the half-full: and he will have patience with them, but they will not always be silent. Two went up: one magnified his holiness and lost it; the other magnified his sins, and they perished; I fast twice in the week, that is, without food and without a woman. What shall I do to have eternal life? That is, as was said above: of such is the kingdom of God; and Nicodemus likewise thought: how can a man be born again? You shall not kill, and the rest: he said these things because he fell in it. When he drew near to Jericho, that is, when he came to the incarnation.

A man named Zacchaeus, that is, he was a Jew, and signifies the Jews; it is interpreted 'justified', just as the Jews justify themselves; because of the crowd, that is, of riches and vices; in the tree, that is, of the cross; half of my goods, that is, of my substance; I give to the poor, that is: break your bread for the hungry; and if I have defrauded anyone, I will restore fourfold: this is said in the Law concerning souls, and in the Gospel it is said concerning every creature. A nobleman, that is, Christ, went into a far country, that is, into heaven; to receive a kingdom for himself, that is, the heavenly kingdom; and to return, for the judgement. Ten servants, that is, the whole human race; ten minas, the ten words of the law; his citizens, that is, the Jews.

They sent an embassy, that is, the killing of the apostles; the first servant and the second, the order of apostles. Each servant's mina, that is, Scripture; and like himself: he found both. The stones will cry out, that is, the gentiles: the Jews were silent. He wept over it: it shows that we should weep for our sins; they will surround you, that is, the Romans surrounded it; on every side, that is, within and without; to the ground, that is, into hell; your children, that is, the powers: what he did by day, by night fell down. Having entered the temple, that is, because he entered the temple on the Lord's day. They sought to destroy him: it shows nine servants who were not denied in their ministries. A certain man, that is, God the Father; planted a vineyard, that is, the Jews; the tenants, that is, the lawgivers; he himself went abroad, that is, he left all in the freedom of their own choice; the first servant, that is, Isaiah; the second, that is, Jeremiah; the third, that is, Daniel; outside the vineyard, that is, outside Jerusalem. What will the lord of the vineyard do? He came and destroyed, that is, the wicked wickedly. He will be shattered, that is, by the cross he will crush his wills; it will grind him to powder, that is, in the vengeance of the cross. Nation against nation, that is, a nation against the Romans; kingdom against kingdom, that is, others against the Romans; terrors, that is, four-horse teams were heard in the air; there will be signs, as there was above Jerusalem a star with a fiery sword; they befall you for a testimony, that is, from the Jews to the gentiles. I will give you a mouth and wisdom: in Moses it is said, God has shown you wisdom.

Not a hair of your head will perish, that is, by mortality. Jerusalem will be trodden down, that is, idols will be worshipped in it; until the times of the gentiles are fulfilled, that is, the Jews converted at the end of the world. Signs in the sun, that is, the letter; the roaring of the sea, that is, the sea of Sodom came to be; it will cast its fish onto the land. Coming in the clouds of heaven, that is, in the prophets and apostles. The fig tree and the trees, that is, the synagogue and men. By day teaching in the temple, that is, he laboured with the Jews; by night on the Mount of Olives, that is, he rested with the gentiles.

A man carrying a jar of water, that is, Moses and John the Baptist; the house of the upper room, that is, the Church; furnished, that is, faith in the Trinity; until the kingdom of God is fulfilled, that is, the great ministry; two cups, one with water, the other with wine, that is, with the mixture of water and wine in the cup: wine with water shows the passion through baptism. Did you lack anything? When he was with them in the flesh, that is, he commanded them to have no care for the world; but when he separates himself from them, [he commands them] to have a single faith; let him buy a sword, that is, the Law; two swords, that is, the two Laws.

The Son of Man seated at the right hand of power: as in "The Lord said to my Lord," and the rest. In a white garment he sent him back to Pilate, that is, in faith in the Trinity: he came to the gentiles, to the people of Israel. They became friends, that is, both peoples [came] to faith in Christ. Herod signifies the people of the gentiles; Pilate, the Jews. Leviathan [...]; Barabbas is called the son of the devil. Weep over yourselves, that is, over your nation; then they will begin to say, that is, the people of Israel; say to the mountains, that is, to the patriarchs; to the hills, that is, to the prophets. Forgive them, that is, let them drink the blood which they shed, so that those who are vessels of wrath may become vessels of mercy. They do not know what they are doing; and if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of majesty: for they did it through ignorance. Today you will be with me in paradise, that is, whoever follows Christ does not have darkness, but the light of life.

Joseph, that is, the people of Israel; spices and ointments, that is, faith, hope, charity; the first day of the week, that is, the Gospel, which dawns through the night of the Old Testament. Women first saw the resurrection: it was fitting that salvation should run first through those through whom death had first hastened in. And behold, two men stood: in Matthew one angel, in Mark a young man, in John two angels, in Luke two men are spoken of, that is, the women made many journeys, and the visions are different; or [taking them] as one, again there was one vision, and the accounts of the evangelists are unlike.

The linen cloths lying alone show that bodies do not need clothing after the resurrection; wondering to himself, that is, that the clothes were left behind. Two of them were going: it shows the gentiles, because he was shown thus to those who were outside, as to those who were inside; a village, that is, the world. Jerusalem, that is, the heavenly [Jerusalem]; a stade, that is, the eighth part of a mile; sixty stades shows the number of days in which the world was made. The name of the village is Emmaus. And he made as if to go farther, that is, to the gentiles; and they knew him in the breaking of bread, and did not know him when they heard [his] preaching. He vanished from their eyes: it shows that we cannot linger in the contemplative [life]; and he was farther from them when they did not know [him], that is, because we can remain longer in the active life; when he opened the Scriptures to us. Peace be with you: now he gathers them into one peace. Why did he not rise and ascend in one place? Because honour went down from Jerusalem to the gentiles. Here the Lord fulfilled what he himself said, Pray for those who persecute [you]: he forgave.
ON THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN.

In the beginning was the Word, that is, because all things are begun and ended in him. The Word of the Father, the Son, with God: because the Son is always with the Father. The Word was God, that is, the Son was God; he was in the beginning with God; all things were made through him, and without him nothing was made: these [are] idols; that is, in him was life, that is, because all things live for him before they come to be; the life was the light of men: Christ is light and life; it shines in the darkness, that is, in the people of the Jews through the Law and the prophets; the Jews did not know him; he was the true light, which enlightens every man, and the rest: the true light enlightens by birth, by nourishing, by living, and through the grace of baptism of the Holy Spirit it enlightens knowledge; he came into the world, the world did not know him, that is, the people of the Jews; a foreign part, some part knew him; he came to his own, to his own nation according to the flesh; who did not receive him; and to those who received him he gave power to become sons of God: through faith they were born of him through the renewal of baptism and the grace of the Holy Spirit. The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us, that is, by the assumption of flesh; we saw his glory, that is, through his transfiguration and resurrection.

He comes after me: it shows the birth according to the flesh; he was made before me, that is, all things were made through him; and because he was before me, and of his fullness we have all received: by birth, by nourishing, by living, grace for grace, for the grace of the Old Testament the grace of the New Testament. Likewise through faith and charity; through the letter of the Law, or prophecy: three ways; through the grace of baptism, eternal grace. The Son who is in the bosom of the Father, that is, in the heart, or in secret. John confessed that he was not the Christ; he did not deny that he was the Forerunner of Christ. Otherwise, it shows the New Testament. And I did not know him: it shows that John did not know that the world was redeemed through the baptism of Christ, for he knew that he was the Son of God and born in the flesh.

Rabbi, where do you dwell? That is, in what teaching are you moved, or do you teach? Come, learn my teaching, for he wants all to come to him; they stayed with him that day: they show the New Testament, or the present life; the tenth hour signifies the evening of the world; the next day he wished to go out into Galilee, that is, after his resurrection to the gentiles; under the fig tree, that is, under the letter of the Law, or the synagogue; heaven opened, that is, to the human race; angels ascending and descending, that is, in the ministry of Christ. On the third day a wedding took place, that is, the third law; the wedding is understood as the joining of the Church with Christ; Mary, Jesus' [mother], at the wedding, shows the synagogue; Jesus and his disciples, a figure of the Church; the wine running short, that is, the failing of the letter of the Law. My hour has not yet come, that is, the time of Christ's passion has not yet come; six water jars, six ages; into wine, Christ; the steward of the feast shows John, because John drank the passion before Christ did; water made wine shows renewal, and the Old Testament [turned] into the New. Otherwise, by the water the baptism of John, by the wine the passion of Christ; likewise by the wine the blood of Christ, as he himself says, his blood is true drink. Keeping the good wine shows a mystery: the mysteries of the Old Testament. By those selling sheep he shows teachers who sell sacred gifts; by the sheep he shows simple men. A whip of cords, that is, punishment for various sins, by which they are cast out of the Church. Jesus did not entrust himself to them, that is, with regard to the flesh. Nicodemus came to him by night: by night it shows the letter of the Law, or ignorance of heart, so that he might be enlightened by the light of the knowledge of God.
