We know that you have come from God: it shows those who received Christ through faith; flesh is born of flesh and blood, so that it may live bodily in the world; again the soul is ineffably reborn of the Holy Spirit, so that it may live for ever.

The Spirit blows where it wills, that is, it enlightens whom it wills, as the Apostle says, For whoever cleaves to Christ is one Spirit. You hear its voice: they show the enlightening of the ear of the heart; hence the prophet says, I will hear what the Lord God speaks in me. What we know we speak, what we have seen we testify; in that he says "We know," it shows [it] through modes of speech, either the whole Trinity, or Christ with the apostles and prophets; we testify, that is, [as one] giving testimony; you do not receive our testimony, that is, you do not believe our preaching. Christ came down from heaven by taking on flesh.

No one ascends to heaven except Christ; with the tree, that is, the Church; as the serpent was lifted up in the desert, so Christ too was lifted up on the wood of the cross: as those bitten by serpents were freed by the sight of the bronze serpent, so too a man bitten by the devil, who believes in the passion of Christ, will be freed. He came into the land of Judaea, into the land of confession; to Aenon, that is, the name of the place where they sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons, from which Gehenna took its name; near Salim, which is interpreted "of peace," which they called Mas, from which the Jebusites took their name; for John was not yet in prison: it shows that the fulfilment of the letter of the Law had not yet come. He must increase, but I must decrease: he who was thought to be a prophet was found to be a prophet. What he has seen and heard, according to his divinity, to this he testifies; according to his divinity no one received his testimony. Here the whole is put for the part; likewise, believe, because God is true.

He had to pass through Samaria: it shows that as he preached to the Jews, so he should preach to the gentiles too; the estate, that is, the field; a spring for flowing, a well for drinking. Jesus wearied from the journey: it shows that he was to come through the incarnation upon the history of the letter of the Law; by the sixth hour is understood the faith of the Samaritans, who were fervent; the woman, that is, the synagogue; to draw water, to learn the history of the letter of the Law; Jesus asks to drink, that is, to ask for the woman's faith; the well is deep, that is, the depth of the mystery of the Law; a spring of water welling up to eternal life, that is, the preaching of the Gospel bubbling up from the mouth of the apostles, or of believers. Five husbands shows the five books of Moses; and the one you have now is not yours shows the book of Joshua. She left her water jar, that is, her former way of life; she went off into the town: it shows the primitive Church [going] as it were to the gentiles, or to the people. Lift up your eyes, that is, the eyes of faith; white harvests, that is, the hearts of the faithful; those who sowed, that is, the prophets; those who reap are the apostles. He stayed with them two days, that is, after the two Testaments were handed down to the Jews; he went off into Galilee, that is, to the gentiles. Here otherwise: those who are dead bodily hear his voice in the future, and are raised. As [the Father] has life in himself, so also the Son: in that it says "he gave to the Son," this is with regard to the flesh. Those who have done good, to the resurrection of life: that is, he who judges himself rises again; and otherwise, those who are dead in sins live to life through conversion to faith; those who did evil here rise to judgement. In that he says, I do nothing of myself, it shows [it] with regard to the body; as I hear, so I judge; my judgement is just; I do not seek my own will, but [the will] of the Father who sent me: here he set down his will on behalf of the members.

If I bear witness about myself, my testimony is not true; as Solomon says, Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth. Nor do they ever hear his voice: it shows the unbelievers, who did not receive his preaching. He went up the mountain with his disciples, that is, trying to climb to a higher life. Philip, that is, to test [him], not to destroy [him]. Five loaves, the five books of Moses; by the barley is understood the harshness of the letter of the Law. Much grass shows the fullness of the people. That nothing of the leftovers be lost, that is, do not cast teaching where it does not build up. He went up the mountain alone, that is, to the Father; the disciples went down to the sea, that is, to the gentiles; they went up into the boat, that is, into the Church. Darkness had come, that is, as the world draws towards evening, or the onslaught of persecution after the ascension of Christ. Rowing, that is, fleeing for refuge to Christ.

Jesus walking on the sea, that is, treading down the vices of the world. The crowds getting into the boat seeking Jesus: it shows that all should seek Christ with their own labour. Among the Hebrews it is called Manu, from which manna took its name; among the Latins this is the living bread, or the body of Christ transfigured in the mystery. A man is raised in three ways, that is, from unbelief to faith, from sin to penance, and on the last day bodily, in the resurrection. I live because of the Father: they show [it] according to the divinity. Scenopegia, that is, the making of tabernacles. You go up to the feast day; I do not go up: you, in whom the world delights; I will not go up, because I am not of the world. In the middle of the feast he went up to Jerusalem, when the zeal of the Jews was burning most fiercely. My teaching is not mine; and if mine, how not mine? It is mine, since it goes out to them from my mouth; it is not mine, because what I have heard from the Father, this I speak to you. Otherwise: according to the flesh it is mine, but according to the divinity it is not mine. I did one work, and you all marvel; I made a whole man well on the sabbath, that is, the whole human race in the New Testament. Do not judge according to appearance, that is, do not show favour to a man's person. You do not know where I am from, that is, according to the flesh.

Yet a little while I am with you: it shows [the time] up to the passion. You will seek me and will not find [me], that is, bodily; and where I am, you cannot come, that is, through unbelief, but only through faith. On the last day of the feast, that is, when the feast of the Jews was over: whoever thirsts, let him come and drink, that is, whoever thirsts for the word of God, let him come and drink the teaching of the Gospel. Rivers from the belly, that is, teaching from the heart; living waters will flow, that is, the preaching of the Gospel, which gives everlasting life. Because Jesus was not yet glorified: it shows the glorification of the passion and resurrection. They went back, each one to his own house, that is, to his own malice.

The woman caught in adultery shows the synagogue, which adulterated the law of Moses and followed the [law] of the traditions of the fathers; or the Church from the gentiles, which, abandoning God, committed fornication with demons. Those who bring her into the middle show the Jews, who are the accusers of the Church of Christ. Moses commanded [us] to stone [such]; what do you say? Testing him for two reasons: if he had said to stone [her], they would have said, "He does not do what he teaches; send her back to us"; if he had said she was not to be stoned, they would have said, "He is an opponent of the Law." Jesus, bending down, that is, from his Father's seat into the world to redeem the sins of the human race; he wrote with his finger on the ground: it shows their sins. He straightened up, to raise up those who were walking in sins. Bending down again, he wrote on the ground: it shows the woman's sins forgiven. Jesus remained alone with the woman in the house, that is, with the Church in the world. Whoever follows me does not walk in darkness: it shows not only the steps of the feet but the disposition of the heart; not in darkness, that is, of ignorance, nor in the darkness of sins; but he will have the light of life, that is, the light of knowledge and everlasting light. I have many things to say and to judge concerning you: it shows that if you believe, I will teach you many things, and if you do not believe, [I have] many things to say to leave you without excuse.

He was a murderer from the beginning: because he killed himself by his pride; otherwise, the first man, whom God created immortal, he made mortal, and through his prompting Abel was killed. Which of you will convict me of sin? Whoever is of God hears the words of God, that is, whoever understands and does [them]. You are a Samaritan and have a demon: what he was not, [he denied] having; and what he was, he assented to by keeping silent. I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks and judges: God the Father. I do not seek [it] as hypocrites do, and judge unjustly. Abraham your father rejoiced to see my day; he saw [it] and was glad, that is, he saw faith in the spirit, and he saw him in the person of the angels: he saw three, he greeted [them] as one, where he said, Turn aside, my lords, to the house of your servant, if I have found favour in your eyes. Amen, amen I say to you: amen doubled has the sense "truly," or "faithfully," announcing the New and Old Testament. Before Abraham, I am: the passage is about the divinity. They took up stones to throw at him, that is, having hearts of stone. Jesus hid himself: it shows that he was hidden from their hearts. And he went out of the temple, that is, out of the people of the Jews. Jesus passed through the midst of them, that is, went away to the gentiles.

He saw a man blind from birth: the blind man signifies the human race. Neither this man sinned nor his parents, so that you may understand what he said, "neither has he sinned": Adam, the first created, had his eyes closed to seeing evil; when he transgressed the commandment of God, he kept his eyes open to evil and shut them to good. What then are the parents but the human race, and the instigators of vices, or are the vices themselves signified? I must work, that is, preach, while it is day, that is, while I am in the world; night will come, that is, the persecution of the apostles, or the persecution of Antichrist; night, when no one can work, that is, after each person's departure. He spat on the ground, that is, the incarnation of Christ. He made mud, he anointed my eyes: it shows that as he formed the first man from the mud of the earth, so through the same kind of mud he re-formed the human race. Go and wash in the pool of Siloam, signifying baptism. By the parents is understood the devil, or the vices: those who said, He is of age, let him speak for himself, who did not want the man to confess Christ. We do not know where this man is from: it shows that they did not know his divinity. For judgement I came into this world: it shows [that] whoever hears the word and receives judgement has received [it] for condemnation. That those who do not see may see: it shows the gentiles, who did not receive the law; and that those who see may become blind, that is, the Jews: those who saw through the law were made blind, because they did not believe in Christ.

Whoever does not enter by the door: it shows bishops who enter by bribes, not by the calling of God or of the people. They are shepherds of the sheep who are [there] for the gain of souls, not for worldly ambition. To him the doorkeeper opens: the first doorkeeper was John, the Forerunner of Christ; [the door] is the divine scripture. He calls by name, that is, the Lord knows who are his; he leads them out, into teaching, or into the kingdom; he goes before them, that is, what he taught he first did as an example; he goes before them into the kingdom of heaven; or also all good teachers go before by their examples. They hear my voice, that is, my teaching; they do not follow a stranger, that is, the faith and teaching of heretics. All who came were thieves and robbers, that is, false prophets, who have been and will be in the time of Antichrist. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved, that is, he who will be saved through the teaching of Christ will go in through penance into the Church, and goes out from the present world to the kingdom of God. Otherwise: go out to fight the heretics. The thief comes only to kill and destroy: these are the ranks of priests who enter for the sake of shameful gain, not for the gain of souls. I came that you may have life, that is, my teaching; and have [it] more abundantly, that is, eternal life. The hireling is one who teaches for earthly gain; he saw the wolf and fled, that is, the devil, or a heretic. I have other sheep which are not of this fold: it shows the gentiles. Let there be one shepherd, that is, the Church and Christ: he is the cornerstone in the middle of the wall, who makes both one.

I have power to lay down my life and to take it up again: it shows [this] on the part of the flesh. What the Father has given me is greater than all: it shows that Christ, or the Spirit of God, is greater than all the works of the world. I said, You are gods: [god] is said in three ways, that is, essentially, he who always is, that is, God; by naming, you are gods; falsely, he calls demons or idols gods. He went away across the Jordan, that is, to the gentiles, where John was first baptizing, and he stayed there: it shows the Church. Lazarus figures the Jews, because the Jews were weak in the faith of Christ; Martha and Mary show the teaching of the good Jews. This sickness is not unto death: it shows that those who are dead to men will live to God. He stayed there two days, that is, the two Testaments. Let us go again into Judaea: the faith turned back to the Jews through Elijah and Enoch at the end of the world. There are twelve hours in the day: the day is Christ; the twelve hours, the twelve apostles. If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble: in the day, that is, in the teaching of Christ or of the apostles, he does not stumble into sin; because he sees the light of this world, that is, he sees Christ through knowledge. If anyone walks in the night, he stumbles: by night are understood the darkness of sins, or ignorance of heart. I was not there: it shows the presence of the flesh. He knew he was dead, that is, because he knows all things. First, in the house of the ruler of the synagogue; second, the widow's son at the gate of the city; third, Lazarus from the tomb: in the house, that is, in the heart; at the gate, that is, in the mouth; in the tomb, that is, in deed. Through these same [three] a man dies, and through the same he will be raised again. Martha, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet him: here Martha signifies the Church, which went to meet Christ through faith. Mary sat at home: it shows the life of contemplation. Whoever believes in me, even if he has died, will live: whether bodily, or [dead] in sins, through penance. Everyone who lives and believes in me: he who here lives in Christ in good works. He will not die for ever. Jesus wept: it shows, as true God and true man, an example of compassion. His hands and feet bound: it shows the bonds of sins. His face bound with a cloth, that is, the veil over the hearts of the Jews. Loose him, that is, through the preaching of the faith. The greater the signs the Jews saw, the more they were blinded. They will take away the place and the nation: the place, Jerusalem, the Romans and gentiles possess, [and the nation], who were scattered through the regions. The leader stated the reasons: it is expedient that one man die, rather than that the whole nation perish: because he had the ministry of God in his hands and the Spirit of God, he spoke this: that he might gather into one the children of God who were scattered, in the whole world.

Martha served: it shows the active life. Lazarus reclining with Jesus signifies the Church. Mary took a pound of ointment: so also the whole world, by which are understood the hearts of the faithful. By the ointment, the fragrance of confession; Mary signifies the Church. She anointed the feet of Jesus, that is, through the confession of penance. The house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment: so also the whole world was filled with the passion and resurrection of Christ. When the crowd heard that Jesus had come, they took branches of palms [and] went out to meet Jesus: it shows that the three, at the second coming after the resurrection, are caught up into the air with the Lord. He found an ass: by the ass it shows the people of the gentiles. He sat on it, that is, through the confession of faith. Do not fear your perdition, because your Saviour comes, daughter of Zion: it shows the congregation of the faithful from Jews and gentiles. The whole world has gone after him, because through his passion and resurrection he redeemed the whole world from sin; and it followed him. They came to Philip and asked to see Jesus: it shows the gentiles converted to the faith through the preaching of the apostles. The grain of wheat holds the figure of Christ: if it dies, it bears many grains; so also Christ [...] multiplied his Church.

I have glorified [it], and I will glorify [it] again, that is, you glorified him in the raising of Lazarus; glorify him again in his own resurrection. The prince of the world is cast out, that is, the devil, thrown out of power over the world through the passion of the cross. Walk while you have the light, that is, while you have Christ with you bodily and spiritually; lest darkness overtake us, that is, the darkness of ignorance and the persecutions of sinners. He hid from them, that is, bodily, or spiritually. Lord, who has believed our report? "Who" is used for rarity, or for difficulty. The report is the faith which we have heard through the Holy Spirit. The arm of the Lord is the Son of God. To whom has it been revealed, that is, some part: from the Jews; revealed from the gentiles, that is, he who believes in me, not only according to the humanity but according to the divinity; otherwise, not only in me but also in the Father, because I am in the Father and the Father in me. He who sees me sees him who sent me; as if he had said plainly: he who has seen that I am true man, and believes that I am true God, sees the Father also according to the divinity.

I did not come to judge but to save the world: it shows that by the shedding of his blood he would redeem the world. I have loved you, because I was in the world. He loved [them] to the end: he gave an example, that all should remain in the truth of God to the end. Supper being ended: it shows the passion of Christ. Just as after supper no meal is taken, so Christ, after he once suffered, does not show that he will suffer again. Rising from supper: it shows our passion, resurrection, or ascension. He laid aside his garments: it shows that his garments were to be laid aside at the cross.

(Here begins the chapter division.) [Taking a towel, he girded himself with the towel, that is, his mortification. He puts water into a basin: it shows the grace of baptism. He began to wash the feet of his disciples and to wipe [them] with the towel: by the washing of the feet the baptism of the apostles is understood; by the wiping with the towel it shows the wiping away of sins through the passion of Christ. You shall never wash my feet: he said this struck with fear. If I do not wash you, you will have no part with me: it shows that whoever is not washed through baptism and through the confession of penance will have no part with the Lord. He took his garments: again it is shown that he will return to the Jews at the end of the world. The servant is not greater than his lord, nor the apostle greater than him who sent him, that is, I suffer and you suffer. Otherwise: if I humble myself even to your feet, so you also humble yourselves to all. He will lift up his heel against me, that is, the heel is the furthest part of the limb.

And with the morsel Satan entered into him, that is, as the Apostle says, he who unworthily receives the Body of the Lord and his blood eats and drinks judgement. A new commandment I give you, that you love one another: in the Old [Testament] it is said, You shall love your friend and hate your enemy. The Lord says, Love your enemies: this is the new commandment. Let not your heart be troubled: here he preaches to the apostles about his passion. Believe in God, and believe in me, because I am the Son of God.

Believe: in my Father's house, that is, in the Church, there are many dwellings, that is, as in one man the senses are divided, so in the Church, which is the body of Christ, there are many graces. I go to prepare a place for you, that is, I will prepare life for you, as the Apostle [says]: we have an advocate with the Father, who intercedes for us. I am the way and the truth and the life: Christ is the way without error, the truth without falsehood; he himself is the life without death.

From now on you know him and have seen him, that is, he whom they knew with the eyes of the body they also knew with the eyes of the heart, according to the divinity, through the illumination of the Holy Spirit. He does greater than these, that is, because Christ healed the woman through the fringe [of his garment], but the apostles will cure the sick through [their] shadow. (Here ends the Passion.

I will ask my Father, and he will give you another Paraclete: by the Spirit received twice, love of God and of neighbour is understood. The Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, that is, he who loves the world does not receive him. I will not leave you orphans, that is, I will not leave you according to the divinity. In that day you will know, that is, in the future, or in the resurrection of Christ. I in the Father, that is, according to the divinity; you in me, because you are my members; and I in you, that is, in the love of your heart. I will manifest myself to him, that is, to those believing in the divinity. We will make our dwelling with him: as he himself says, Where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I also, and the rest. My peace I give you, that is, as I patiently endure all things, so you too have patience. My peace I leave you, that is, as I have suffered, so you too will suffer. Not as the world gives peace do I give to you: the world gives a broken peace, God gives an eternal one. The prince of the world comes to me, he finds nothing in me, that is, the devil came to the cross and found no sin in the Lord: he sought to capture, he was captured by him. As the Father commanded me, so I do: the Father sent him to shed his blood for the human race, and so he did. I am the true vine, from which blood and water flow; and my Father is the vinedresser, that is, the cultivator of the Church. These branches, that is, the apostles, or the faithful of the Church: as the branch cannot bear fruit of itself unless it remains in the vine, so also no one bears fruit unless he remains in Christ.

In this my Father is glorified, that you bring forth first fruit, that is, as I have made preaching and the passion bear fruit, so you too do. As the Father has loved me, so I too have loved you, that is, as the Father sent me to preach and to suffer, so I too send you. No one has greater love, and the rest: love is stronger than death; through love I suffer for you, and you suffer for the Church. All that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you, that is, the precepts of the Gospel. I chose you out of the world, that is, out of worldly deeds. You are not of the world, that is, because you do not love the world. As Solomon says, Such is the adulterous woman, who, when she has eaten, wipes her mouth and says, I have done no evil: she figures the Church from the gentiles, which through confession has wiped itself clean of the uncleanness of sins. From the beginning you have been with me, that is, from the beginning of the preaching.

If I do not go away, the Paraclete will not come to you. When the Paraclete comes, he will convict the world of sin, that is, whoever does not believe in me, let him believe through the preaching of the Gospel; and of judgement, because the prince of the world has been judged. He will convict of sin, that is, so that through your preaching they may be turned to repentance; of justice, so that as one loves his neighbour, he may also love God with his whole heart; of judgement, so that whatever you wish men to do to you, you also do to them: for this is the Law and the Prophets.

A little while and you will not see me, that is, while I lay in the tomb; again a little while and you will see me, that is, through the resurrection. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but will show you plainly of the Father, that is, through the resurrection. On that day you will ask in my name, that is, because I ascend to the Father, rising again through [my] power. The Father loves you, because you love me. I leave the world and go to the Father, that is, as to the presence of the body, for according to the divinity he does not leave the world. You have distress, that is, tribulation from worldly men. I have overcome the world, that is, I have bound the strong man in the world, who is the devil.

The hour has come, Father, to glorify your Son, that is, through the resurrection, that the Son may glorify you, that is, that through the Son they may be converted and believe. I have glorified you upon the earth, that is, I have made [you] known to all; with you. I have manifested your name to men: he showed that according to the divinity he was with the Father, and bodily on earth. Those whom you gave me out of the world were yours, in foreknowledge they were yours from the beginning; you gave them to me, that is, for teaching; and they have kept your word, that is, they remained in the faith. I pray for them, not for the world, because God knows who are his. All that is yours is mine, and what is mine is yours; and I am glorified in them, that is, I have been made manifest among these same gentiles, that is, because they believed in me. I am in the world bodily, and I am not in the world bodily; and for them I sanctify myself, that is, through martyrdom and resurrection. The glory which you gave me I have given them, that is, the divine precepts. He went out with his disciples across the brook Kidron: this shows the onslaught of persecution. Again Jesus crossing with his disciples, that is, from the world to the Father, and from the Jews to the gentiles. They came with lanterns and torches, that is, they kindled for themselves a penal light. They led him to Annas: Annas is interpreted 'grace of God', who by the grace of God had received the chief priesthood; but that doorkeeper who was seen, who brought Peter into the courtyard, signifies the early Church. He reproached him because he had said he was the Son of God; surely, he did not think it robbery to be equal to God, but emptied himself and took the form of a servant.

Jesus carrying his cross: he gave an example, as he himself said, Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, and the rest. Two thieves were crucified with Jesus: the one who remained in his faithlessness shows the Jews; the one who confessed signifies the gentiles. It was written in the inscription, King of the Jews, that is, king of those who confess. They made four parts of the garments of Jesus: four soldiers, that is, the four evangelists; the garments divided, that is, the preaching, incarnation, passion and resurrection, which they preached in the four parts of the world. But the seamless tunic, woven from the top, shows that the divinity in the Father and the Son is inseparable. Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: this shows that catholic men do not tear apart the unity of the divinity.

Woman, behold your son; to the disciple, Behold your mother: here he entrusted the virgin [to him], so that he might keep her undefiled. They did not break the legs of Jesus, that is, what had been prefigured before through the lamb in Egypt: not raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted with fire, shows the passion of Christ; the staff in the hand shows the cross of Christ, [the passage] from the world to the Father; you shall not break [a bone] of it shows that the cross of Christ was not to be broken. They pierced his side with a lance, that the Scripture might be fulfilled: They looked on him whom they pierced.

There came out blood and water: as Eve was taken from the side of Adam, so from the side of Christ came out the redemption of the Church: through the blood, remission; through the water, baptism. Two disciples running, Peter and John, show two peoples running: the Jews through the letter of the Law, the gentiles through the law of nature.

John ran ahead more quickly, saw the linen cloths lying, and did not go in: the Jews through the Law and the Prophets saw that Christ would come, and did not receive his coming. Peter came following him, saw the linen cloths, and went in: this shows the gentiles, who [believed] in the coming of Christ, or his teaching. By the linen cloths the incarnation of Christ is understood; by the face-cloth the mystery of the divinity is understood. The face-cloth not with the linen cloths, but rolled up separately in one place, shows that the divinity is far removed from human senses; in one place, who are universal. Then the other disciple also went in, who had come first to the tomb: this shows the Jews returned to the faith at the end of the world. Angels sitting at the head and at the feet show the beginning and the end.

Mary said, I do not know where they have laid him: this shows [her thinking] according to the flesh. She loved the Lord, and through faith believed; what Mary said shows the thought behind the words, because through love of neighbour a man knows God. Jesus said, Do not touch me, that is, in your heart; I have not yet ascended for you, through the divinity. The disciples fishing all night caught nothing: the fishermen are the teachers of old; the night shows that before the coming of Christ no one came to perfection through the preaching of the old Law. But when morning came: this shows the coming of Christ accomplished. Cast to the right side, that is, cast the preaching among the gentiles. For Peter was naked, that is, they were naked of the faith of Christ; he girded himself with his tunic, the faith of the Church; he threw himself into the sea, that is, into the turmoil and bitterness of the world, through love of Christ. The other disciples came in the boat, that is, in the Church, treading down the turmoil of the world. They saw coals, and a fish, and bread laid out: by the fish he shows faith, by the coals the warmth of charity, by the bread the divine word. Dragging the net to land: by the shore he shows the end of the world; full of large fish, that is, the fullness and greatness of the Church, through the remission of sins; through three he shows the Trinity. The net undivided and not torn, that is, the Church incorrupt in the future. Jesus ate after the resurrection: this shows the true incarnation of the body, so that believers might believe.

Jesus said, Simon [son] of John, do you love me? This shows that, as he denied three times, so he should three times confess the faith of the Trinity. Feed my sheep, that is, in the Church. Jesus entered when the doors were shut: this shows that he entered with the doors shut, [as he left] the womb [closed] (so also all the saints after the resurrection put on a spiritual body, and can enter anywhere without [hindrance]); hence whole and incorrupt in marriage. Three bear witness to this statement.

The disciple whom Jesus loved: the second sign is that Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, he drew wine from water: the work prepared shows the virginity of John, because a bride was joined to him; the testimony by which Jesus entrusted his mother to John. Mary figures the Church, John the primacy; as John was a virgin in marriage, so he was also incorrupt in death. John narrates a genealogy of the divinity, for the others narrate of the man: of the divinity John says, In the beginning was the Word. He lay upon the breast of Jesus, and the knowledge of the divinity which had been in the breast of Jesus passed up into John from the joining of the two breasts. A tree grafted onto another bears the fruit of the other tree in which it is planted. If according to the order of the canon this book ought to be placed before Matthew, yet it has been placed in the last part because first the earth was sanctified, then water, and after that, last of all, fire, because it is brighter and finer; likewise in the likeness of the two laws, that is, the old and the new: the old was handed down first, yet the new is brighter and greater, because it distinguishes heavenly things, and is more abundant. That is what pertains to the Gospel of John from the things said above.
